This <term>Vedha</term><note>Obstruction; a concept where the positive or negative effect of a planet in a certain house is canceled or "blocked" by another planet in a corresponding house.</note> is said to occur from the sign occupied by the planet. Others say it occurs from the birth sign <insert>or the name sign</insert>. In the case of a "reverse obstruction," the auspicious and inauspicious results are flipped. For example: if the Sun is in the 6th house, it is auspicious; however, if any planet other than Saturn is in the 12th house, then the Sun is no longer auspicious. Conversely, if the Sun is in the 12th house, it is inauspicious; but if a planet other than Saturn is in the 6th house, then the Sun's inauspiciousness is removed.

By worshipping them <note>the deities or planets</note>, by bowing to the primordial gods, by listening to the stories of the virtuous, by looking upon the faces <note>of the holy</note>, by performing fire sacrifices <term>homa: a ritual where offerings are made into a consecrated fire</term>, by chanting prayers, by reciting the sacred scriptures, and by giving charity, the sky-traveling planets do not afflict embodied beings. For children up to eight years of age, the results <note>of planetary movements</note> are felt by the father; after marriage, the ripening of the fruit of these actions is understood to affect the husband of a woman.

## Concerning the Transit of Planets

The transit of a planet through the birth constellation <term>janma-nakshatra: the star sign the moon was in at birth</term> causes great distress. An eclipse occurring in the birth constellation, or in the tenth or nineteenth constellation from it, is also painful. If an eclipse occurs in the zodiac sign occupied by the Sun at birth, it brings sorrow.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

<unclear>If</unclear> an eclipse occurs in the lunar mansion <note>Nakshatra</note> in which a king’s coronation was performed, it causes the destruction of the kingdom, the loss of allies, or even death. Likewise, an eclipse occurring in the 7th, 16th, or 25th lunar mansion from the birth star is considered painful. To mitigate this, one should perform prayers <note>Japa</note>, fire sacrifices <note>Homa</note>, and pacification rituals, or the donation of a golden serpent <note>Nagadana</note>, as prescribed in the traditional treatises.

Now, the strength of the stars <term>Tarabala: the strength derived from the position of the stars relative to one's birth star</term> is explained. From the eighth day of the dark fortnight <note>Krishna Paksha</note> until the end of the new moon, the strength of the stars is paramount. Beyond that, the strength of the Moon <note>Chandra-bala</note> should be considered for all auspicious activities. The nine stars are: Birth, Wealth, Danger, Prosperity, Obstacle, Realization, Destruction, Friend, and Great Friend. Their results are exactly as their names suggest. 

Even if the strength of the stars is lacking, the Moon is auspicious and powerful during the bright fortnight. Conversely, if the stars are auspicious during the dark fortnight, the Moon may still be unfavorable. Some say the Moon has no strength in the dark fortnight, and the stars have no strength in the bright fortnight. When the master of the house is away in another country, the wife may perform all necessary duties; here too, they say the strength of the "Lord of the Stars" <note>the Moon</note> is what matters. 

Some authorities claim that in both fortnights, the strength of the Moon combined with the strength of the stars should always be considered. Others argue that even in the dark fortnight, the Moon's strength is primary, not the stars. They say that whether the Moon is full or waning, it is the Moon alone that allows all works to be accomplished. Without the "Lord of Herbs" <note>a poetic name for the Moon</note>, the strength of the stars yields no desired fruit in either fortnight. Just as a man cannot succeed in the world without a wife, so too is the Moon necessary for success. Despite these various opinions and doubts raised by such sayings, the previously mentioned rule remains the most pleasing and correct. One should count from the birth star to the star of the day...

Now, the remedy for the stars: In the first cycle <note>the first 9 stars from the birth star</note>, the "Death," "Obstacle," and "Adversary" stars must be avoided. In the second cycle <note>stars 10-18</note>, one must avoid the first quarter of the "Obstacle" star, the fourth quarter of the "Adversary" star, and the third quarter of the "Death" star respectively. In the third cycle <note>stars 19-27</note>, all stars are considered auspicious. 

The Moon derives its strength from the strength of the stars; the Sun derives its strength from the strength of the Moon; and all other planets derive their strength from the Sun. Even so, the lunar strength is considered the most important. 

Now, regarding the transit of Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>: the lunar influence is primary regarding one's own birth constellation. Now, regarding the strength of the Moon: when the Moon is in its sign of exaltation, its "moolatrikona" <note>a specific high-potency zodiacal zone</note>, or a friend's sign, even a poor stellar position is mitigated. From the birth sign, the 6th and 5th positions are auspicious in the bright fortnight; in the dark fortnight, the 3rd is auspicious. During the bright fortnight, the Moon is generally auspicious; if the Moon is poorly placed during the dark fortnight, the entire fortnight is considered difficult. If the conditions are reversed, the results are reversed, as shown in the chart.

If a constellation is joined by Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note>, Mars, or Saturn, or corrupted by the "Mars-Cycle" <note>a specific malefic calculation</note>, or struck by meteors or eclipses, it becomes "afflicted" and loses its natural character. A constellation free from such disturbances is "healthy," bringing happiness and strength. If six of these limbs are afflicted, the person is destroyed; if three are afflicted along with others, even a lord of the earth <note>a king</note> suffers. 

In auspicious works like marriage or post-conception rituals <note>*Garbhadhana*</note>, the strength of the Moon must be calculated according to the husband's transit for the woman's benefit. In the rite of marriage <note>*Panigrahana*</note> for a man and woman, the strength of their parents must also be considered. Likewise, for the head of a family, the eldest earning member, or the commander of an army, the strength of the Moon must be examined. For the leader of a house-building project or for followers in a war, the Moon's strength is vital. 

However, some say the Moon's strength need not be considered for certain acts: for one seeking firewood, for a pregnant woman's cravings <note>*Dohada*</note>, for a beggar, for the final stages of a sacrifice, or for one performing the "Vow of a Thousand Moons" <note>a ritual performed upon seeing 1000 full moons in one's life</note>. 

Now, the States of the Moon <note>*Chandra-avastha*</note>: Take the number of elapsed constellations starting from Ashvini, multiply by 60, add the elapsed minutes <note>*ghatis*</note> of the current constellation, multiply by 4, and divide by 45. The quotient indicates the current state: 
1. Travel, 2. Destruction, 3. Death, 4. Victory, 5. Laughter, 6. Sexual pleasure, 7. Play, 8. Equilibrium, 9. Liberation, 10. Fever...

<note>The table above is a 9x9 grid representing the Sarvatobhadra Chakra. The outer edges contain vowels and Nakshatras (lunar mansions). The inner squares contain Tithis (lunar days like Nanda, Bhadra), weekdays, and Zodiac signs (represented by numbers 1-12). "Vedha" refers to the 'piercing' or aspectual interference of a planet upon a specific point in the grid.</note>

Loss occurs in the "unfailing field" <note>original: "amogha-kshetra"</note>; through the vowels, disease and fear arise. When a Zodiac sign is pierced <term>Vedha: an astrological 'hit' or aspect from a planet</term>, great obstacles occur. If five points are pierced simultaneously, the subject does not survive. The method of piercing is shaped like the Bharani constellation. A planet in Krittika pierces Taurus, the Nanda and Bhadra lunar days, the letter 'Ta', Shravana, Vishakha, and Libra. A planet in Rohini pierces the letters 'Va', 'Au', and 'U', as well as the Ashwini and Swati constellations, the letter 'Ra', Gemini, Virgo, and the intercalary constellation Abhijit. 

Regarding the specific movement in Rohini: when a planet is retrograde <note>moving backward from our perspective on Earth</note> in Rohini, the piercing goes toward Ashwini. When the planet is moving fast <note>accelerated motion</note> in Rohini, the piercing is toward Swati on the left. When the planet is slow-moving in Rohini, Abhijit is pierced. If the piercing is by a benefic planet <note>such as Jupiter or Venus</note>, the result is auspicious; if by a malefic planet <note>such as Saturn or Mars</note>, the result is wicked.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments
<note>original: "Muhurta Sindhu," a classical Sanskrit treatise on electional astrology.</note>

## The Three-Flagged Chart
<note>original: "Tripataki." This chart is used to visualize the aspects or "piercings" (vedha) of planets across different zodiac signs.</note>

By placing the planets according to their current zodiacal positions, one determines victory or fear based on which signs are "pierced" by their influence. The planets should be positioned according to the specific day for which the good or bad results are desired.

## The Solar Fire of Time
<note>original: "Surya Kalanal." A diagnostic chart used to predict the outcome of specific events based on the Sun's position relative to one's birth star.</note>

Counting from the Sun's current constellation to the constellation of one's own name: if it falls at the "base," there is an obstacle to the desired goal; if on the two "horns," there is a breaking of disease <note>recovery from illness</note>; if on the "shackles" or "points," death is indicated. In the remaining positions, one finds victory, profit, and the fulfillment of desired goals. This should be considered in matters of illness, debates, battles, and journeys.

## The Lunar Fire of Time
<note>original: "Chandra Kalanal." Similar to the solar version, but calculated using the Moon's position to determine daily fluctuations in fortune.</note>

## The Fort Diagram <note>Sanskrit: Kota-chakram. A specialized diagram used to predict the outcome of conflicts, illnesses, or the stability of a person's "fortress" (life/body).</note>

In this diagram: Krittika, Tishya, Ashlesha, Magha, Purva Phalguni, Bharani, Swati, Vishakha, Anuradha, Abhijit, Shravana, Dhanishta, Ashwini, and Bhadrapada <note>These are abbreviations for the 27/28 Nakshatras or lunar mansions.</note>—these 12 are placed on the **outer** boundary. Rohini, Purva Ashadha, Uttara Phalguni, Chitra, Jyeshtha, Uttara Ashadha, Shatabhisha, and Revati—these 8 are in the **intermediate** section. Mrigashira, Ardra, Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Mula, Pushya, Purva Bhadrapada, and Uttara Bhadrapada—these are in the **center**. In this system, if a malefic planet <note>A planet with a negative influence, like Mars or Saturn.</note> is on the outer boundary, it is auspicious; however, a malefic influence in the center causes hardship. Further details should be sought from other texts. This concludes the section on planetary transits.

### The Ocean of Auspicious Moments.

...the lineage meets its end; if the first menses are seen at an inauspicious time, it brings fear. In such cases, one should perform a pacification ceremony <note>Shanti: a ritual to avert evil or bad luck</note> for the women. Until the purification is complete, the husband should avoid physical union, as prescribed by the scriptures. 

#### The Procedure for This
The woman, adorned and in her menstrual period, should be seated in a pleasant part of the house illuminated by a lamp. One should offer betel nuts along with sesame seeds and flour cakes to other women, and worship with the mantras of the twice-born <note>Brahmins</note>. The wise man should place her upon a heap of consecrated grains, recite prayers for a holy day <note>Punyahavachanam</note>, and feed the Brahmins.

#### Her Purification
On the fourth day, she becomes touchable by her husband. On the fifth day, she becomes pure for rites concerning the gods and the ancestors.

#### The Pacification according to the Ritual Manuals
One should perform a fire sacrifice <note>Homa</note> with one hundred and eight offerings of clarified butter <note>Ghee</note>, Durva grass, and unbroken rice. One should also donate gold, cows, and land; further details on this can be found in the specialized treatises.

#### Her Religious Duties and Restrictions
A woman in her menstrual period should not stay in the same common room. She must not touch those of the lowest castes, nor indeed should she touch anyone at all. She should not speak loudly, nor should she brush her teeth. A menstruating woman should not look at the planets or stars. She must avoid applying collyrium <note>eye salve</note>, massaging with oil, bathing, or going on a journey. She must avoid cutting her nails, or binding ropes and palm leaves. She should not eat cooked rice <note>Odan: specifically boiled grain</note> and should drink water only from her cupped hands. She must strictly avoid bathing for cleanliness, singing, weeping, laughing, and especially sleeping during the day. Furthermore, she must avoid cleaning her teeth with wood, sexual intercourse, eating meat, speaking excessively, and the worship of deities. With all effort, she must avoid touching or speaking with another menstruating woman. She must also avoid the clothes discarded by another in that state. After her bath at the end of the period, the woman should not touch another man. She should gaze upon the Lord of Uma <note>Shiva</note> and then drink the Five Products of the Cow <note>Brahmakurcha or Panchagavya: a purifying mixture of milk, curd, ghee, urine, and dung</note>. Whatever kind of man a woman sees first after her ritual bath, she will bear a son of that likeness; therefore, she should look upon her own husband.

#### The Bath after the Appearance of Menses

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

|| In the lunar mansions of Swati, Ashwini, Mrigashira, Anuradha, Dhanishta, the three later mansions (Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada), Rohini, and Jyeshtha; on an auspicious lunar day, an auspicious weekday, and under an auspicious rising sign, a woman quickly attains pregnancy. || <term>Garbhadhana</term> <note>The ritual of conception, the first of the sixteen Hindu sacraments (Samskaras).</note> ||

One should avoid the three types of "junction points" (Gandanta), the birth star, and the stars Bharani, Ashlesha, and Revati. Avoid the day of an eclipse, the astrological yogas of Vyatipata and Vaidhriti, days of ancestral offerings (Shraddha), and daytime. Avoid the first half of the Parigha yoga, stars struck by natural portents, the eighth sign from the birth moon, the houses of malefic planets, the Vishti (Bhadra) period, and the 4th, 8th, 14th, and 6th lunar days. Avoid the twilight hours and the weekdays of the Sun, Mars, and Saturn. The fourth night after the onset of menstruation is also considered inauspicious.

The mansions Uttara (the three), Mrigashira, Hasta, Anuradha, Rohini, Swati, Shravana, Dhanishta, and Shatabhisha are favorable. When the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, or 8th houses are occupied by benefics, and the 3rd, 6th, and 11th houses are occupied by malefics; and when the Sun, Mars, and Jupiter are in favorable positions in the rising sign, and the Moon is in an odd-numbered sign or its sub-division (Navamsha), it is auspicious. The mansions Chitra, Pushya, and Tishya are considered middling.

|| Now, some specific details ||
Regarding the sacraments of the womb starting from conception: even if the planetary transits (<term>Gocharo</term> <note>The movement of planets relative to one's birth chart.</note>) are favorable for the woman, one should not attempt conception on the woman's birthday, in a river, at midnight, or during the dawn. Likewise, one should not proceed when the lord of the rising sign is combust (too close to the Sun) or on the eighth lunar day. Conception on even-numbered nights results in sons, while odd-numbered nights result in daughters.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

## 2. The Rite for Ensuring a Male Child <note>Sanskrit: Pumsavana; a ritual performed during pregnancy to pray for a healthy male heir and the physical well-being of the fetus.</note>
This ritual should be performed in the second or third month of pregnancy. It should be carried out once the pregnancy is clearly visible, or it may be performed alongside the Hair-Parting ritual. Alternatively, some authorities state this must be performed for every pregnancy. 

The auspicious lunar mansions <term>Nakshatras: the 27 divisions of the sky</term> for this are: Hasta, Mrigashira, Shravana, Pushya, Mula, Tishya (Pushya), Anuradha, Ashwini, and Purva Bhadrapada. One should avoid the "Empty" lunar days <note>Rikta Tithis: the 4th, 9th, and 14th days of the lunar fortnight, considered unlucky for new beginnings</note>, the first day of the fortnight, and the new/full moon days. 

The preferred days of the week are Sunday, Tuesday, and Thursday. The ritual should be done in a "masculine" zodiac sign <note>odd-numbered signs like Aries or Gemini</note>, excluding Gemini, and the rising sign should be occupied by its own lord. The 6th, 8th, and 12th houses should be free of planets, while malefic planets should be in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses. Jupiter is auspicious in the 1st, 4th, 5th, 7th, 9th, 10th, or 11th houses. 

Regarding this, the sage Parashara says: For the merchant and laboring classes <note>Vaishyas and Shudras</note>, this may be performed in the seventh month, and the Revati star is also considered acceptable. 

**The effects of the weekday on this ritual:**
If performed on a Saturday, it leads to death; on a Monday, loss of breast milk; on a Wednesday, the child may die or the woman may become barren like a "crow-barren" woman <note>a metaphor for a woman who bears only one child</note>; on a Friday, only daughters may be born; on Sunday, Tuesday, or Thursday, a son is obtained. 
<insert>In this same context, the ritual for preventing miscarriage (Anavalobhana) is also mentioned.</insert>

## 3. The Hair-Parting Rite <note>Sanskrit: Simanta; a ritual where the husband parts the wife's hair, intended to keep the mother-in-waiting cheerful and protect the fetus.</note>
This is performed in the fourth, sixth, or eighth month when the planetary lord of that month is strong and the Moon and birth stars of the couple are favorable. 

**Auspicious Stars:** Tishya, Hasta, Pushya, Shravana, Mrigashira, Revati, Rohini, and the three "Uttara" stars. 
**Avoid:** The 4th, 8th, 9th, 6th, 12th, and 30th (New Moon) lunar days. 
**Favorable:** The 4th and 14th days of the bright fortnight are good. 
**Days:** Sunday, Tuesday, and Thursday. 
In the dark fortnight, the 10th day is avoided. 

The rising sign should be masculine. Benefic planets should be in the 1st, 4th, 5th, 7th, 9th, or 10th houses, and malefic planets in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th. The Moon should not be in the 1st, 6th, 8th, or 12th houses. The rising sign should not be the 8th sign from the birth sign or birth ascendant. Even a single malefic planet in the 5th, 8th, or 12th house can cause injury to the fetus. However, if the lord of the 8th house from the rising sign is in a central house <term>Kendra</term> and aspected by benefics, the faults are removed. 

Some say this should be done under the same stars as the previous ritual. It should be performed during the middle two quarters of the star's duration. Both rituals should be done during the day; however, for the merchant and laboring classes, they may be done at night. This rite is performed only once <note>i.e., only during the first pregnancy</note>. A penance <term>Prayashchitta</term> is also prescribed here regarding food.

## Additional Duties for the Pregnant Woman
She should not sit on charcoal, ashes, bones, skull fragments, chaff, or winnowing baskets...

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

A woman should not sit upon a mortar, a pestle, or a grinding stone <note>These are heavy stone kitchen implements used for processing grain</note>, nor upon husks or chaff. Similarly, she should not sit upon a broom or a lump of dried cow dung. She must not bathe in water while naked, nor should she scratch the earth with charcoal, a pot-shard, or her fingernails. She should not break pieces of straw or wood <note>literally "limbs of the body of Kali," referring to the personification of discord and misfortune</note>. She should not have her hair disheveled or be without clothing. She must not sleep during the twilight hours after eating, nor should she utter inauspicious words. She should not go to a deserted house or sit beneath a tree.

A pregnant woman <term>Garbhini; a woman carrying a child</term> should always avoid foods that are excessively pungent, sharp, astringent, very hot, or salty. She must avoid physical exertion and sexual intercourse. She should abandon the climbing of elephants, horses, mountains, or upper stories of palaces. She must avoid strenuous exercise, walking too fast, and riding in carriages. She should avoid grief, bloodletting <note>a traditional medical practice</note>, rash acts, and the "cockerel" sitting posture <note>a specific yogic or physical squat</note>. She should avoid daytime naps and staying awake late at night.

Turmeric, vermilion, red lead <note>Sindoor</note>, kohl, the bodice <note>Kurpasaka; a fitted blouse</note>, betel leaf, and auspicious ornaments are beneficial. She should always maintain her hair, wear braids, and adorn her hands and ears. A pregnant woman who desires a long life for her husband should always wear these. Although some authorities say she should not wear them, this should be ignored as it contradicts many other sacred texts. These rules must be strictly followed after the <term>Simantonnayana; the 'Parting of the Hair' ritual performed in the late stages of pregnancy</term>.

**Duties for the Husband of a Pregnant Woman:**
The husband of a pregnant woman—provided his own father is still living—should not perform tonsure <note>ritual head-shaving</note>, the offering of funeral cakes <term>Pinda-dana; offerings to the deceased</term>, or any funeral rites. He should also not partake in a funeral feast from the seventh month of pregnancy onwards. The prohibition of "tonsure" includes the cutting of hair in general. The prohibition of offering funeral cakes applies to cases other than the offerings made to one's own parents. Bathing in the ocean is also forbidden, as is going on a pilgrimage, except for a pilgrimage to Gaya <note>a holy city famous for ancestral rites</note>.

Regarding the "Parting of the Hair" ceremony, there is a prohibition against performing it during one's birth-star <note>Janma-nakshatra; the lunar mansion the person was born under</note>. However, according to the sage Vasistha: "The birth-star is auspicious for the first feeding of a child, for the thread ceremony, and for the coronation of a king, provided it is not a cruel day; but for marriage, the Parting of the Hair ceremony, and journeys, it is considered inauspicious."

**Now begins the Worship of Vishnu.**

For ten days, the delivery chamber should be specially protected with weapons, fire, charcoal of Tinduka wood, full water-pots, and lamps. With a pestle and water-barriers, and after the recitation of "Auspicious Day" <note>Punyahavachana: a consecration ritual</note>, she should be made to enter. **Now, the Birth Rite <term>Jatakarma: a rite of passage performed at birth</term>.**

Upon hearing that a son is born, the father should perform a bath with his clothes on. This must be done even at night. The ancestral offerings <term>Shraddha</term> and other gifts should be made in gold. If it cannot be done at that moment, it should be done at the end of the impurity period <term>Sutaka</term>. At that time, the constellations should be the Soft, Fixed, Movable, or Swift ones. It should be performed on a favorable weekday and lunar day, in an Ascendant where Jupiter and Venus are in the center houses. **Now, the duties following the Birth Rite:**

Having examined the Ascendant, one should perform planetary charity and chanting <term>Japa</term> to remove any ill-effects of the planets. If the child is born under the Mula constellation or similar difficult stars, the father should see the child's face only after performing the pacification rites. **Now, the worship of the Birth Deities:**

On the first day, or the tenth, or always, one should observe the three-fold purification during the birth-impurity. This applies to the birth of a son, and also on the fifth and eighth days. On the first day, the "Prosperity Rite" <term>Abhyudayika</term> is performed. On the fifth day, the worship of the Birth-Goddess and Shashthi <note>the protector of children</note>. On the tenth day, the offering of oblations. On the eighth day, the giving of food. Now—

# Ocean of Auspicious Times

->**Breastfeeding**<-
The first feeding of breast milk should occur under the following lunar mansions <note>Nakshatras</note>: the three "Later" mansions <note>Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada</note>, Rohini, Ashwini, Revati, Pushya, Tishya <note>another name for Pushya</note>, Anuradha, Hasta, Chitra, Mrigashirsha, Dhanishta, Shravana, and Shatabhishak. It should be done on an auspicious lunar day <note>Tithi</note>, an auspicious day of the week, and during a stable zodiacal sign <note>Sthira Lagna</note>.

**Dietary Regimen for the Postpartum Woman**
The rules for the mother's diet follow those prescribed for the child's first feeding of solid food <note>Annaprashana</note>, provided it is an auspicious lunar day and free from harmful astrological combinations <note>Duryoga</note>.

**Medicinal Decoction for the Postpartum Woman**
<margin>Library of Pratap Maharaj, Kolhapur</margin>
The medicinal drink <note>Kwatha</note> should be administered on days and under lunar mansions prescribed by medical treatises <note>Bhaishajya</note>, ensuring the timing is free from harmful combinations for both the mother and the infant.

**The Postpartum Ritual Bath**
The ritual bath should be taken under Hasta, Mrigashirsha, Anuradha, Rohini, Revati, Ashwini, or the three "Later" mansions. It should occur on a lunar day other than the "Empty" days <note>Rikta Tithis: 4th, 9th, and 14th</note>, in a zodiacal sign where the fifth house is pure <note>Panchama-shuddhi</note>, joined by beneficial planets, free from defects, and on an auspicious day of the week.

**Results of Bathing under the Shatabhishak Mansion**
Women who bathe when the Moon is in the Shatabhishak mansion may become widows or unfortunate for seven subsequent births. If a woman must bathe during Shatabhishak, she should devotedly worship her husband and perform rituals to balance the good and bad effects.

**The Naming Ceremony**
The naming ceremony <note>Namakarana</note> should be performed at the end of the birth-impurity period <note>Sutaka</note>, according to the customs of one's own family.
**The Sage Vyasa says:** "Some sages desire the naming on the tenth day; others say the twelfth; others when a full month has passed."
Some wise men say it may be done on the eighteenth day.
**The Sage Brihaspati says:** "On the twelfth day, or on an auspicious day of birth, or on the sixteenth, twentieth, or twenty-second day, according to the order of the social classes <note>Varnas</note>."

The ceremony should occur under these lunar mansions: Mrigashirsha, Revati, Chitra, Anuradha, the three "Later" mansions, Rohini, Hasta, Ashwini, Tishya, Abhijit, Pushya, Shravana, Dhanishta, and Shatabhishak. Choose an auspicious day, avoiding the following: the solar transition <note>Sankranti</note>, the new moon <note>Amavasya</note>, "broken" lunar days <note>Paksha-chidra</note>, "empty" days <note>Rikta</note>, "full" days <note>Purna</note>, and specific astrological hazards like Vyatipata, Vaidhriti, Shakuni, and Vishti-Karana.

It should be done in an auspicious rising sign <note>Lagna</note>, specifically a stable sign <note>Sthira Lagna</note>, ensuring the eighth house is pure. The 8th and 12th houses are generally not auspicious. Benefic planets should be in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, or 9th houses. Malefic planets should be in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses. The strength of the Moon and the birth star <note>Tara-bala</note> must be considered for both the father and the son. It should be performed in the forenoon. The name should be given according to the social class, ending in suffixes like *Sharman* (for Brahmins), *Varman* (for Kshatriyas), *Gupta* (for Vaishyas), or *Dasa* (for Shudras).

**Names According to the Month of Birth**
The names for the months are: Krishna, Ananta, Achyuta...

These are the names of the Lord to be used in sequence: Vaikuntha, Janardana, Upendra, Yajñapurusha, Vasudeva, Hari, Yogisha, and Pundarikaksha <note>These are various names for Vishnu, the Preserver deity</note>. Here, the sequence begins with the month of Margashirsha <note>approximately November-December</note>. One should also assign a name based on the birth star <term>Nakshatra</term> for the purpose of identification. 

Regarding the formation of the name: the name should begin with the specific letter associated with the birth star. In the constellations of Rohini, Revati, Magha, Mrigashirsha, Jyeshtha, and Chitra, the first vowel should be lengthened. In the constellations of Dhanishtha, Shravana, and Ashvini, the final vowel is modified. For the remaining stars, the final vowel of the two names should be followed by a visarga <note>a Sanskrit phonetic marker resembling a colon</note>. 

Some authorities state the name should be connected to the family deity <term>Kuladevata</term>, while others say it should be connected to one's Guru. In all cases, one should avoid names with two or four syllables that end in the letters 'L' or 'R'. The father should whisper the name into the child's right ear. When performing this ceremony at the end of the birth-impurity period <term>Sutaka</term>, one need not worry about the restrictions of intercalary months <term>Malamasa</term> or the setting of the planets Venus and Jupiter. However, if the ceremony is performed after the prescribed time has passed, all such astrological factors must be carefully considered.

### Special Instructions Regarding Girls
A wise man, seeking the welfare of his family, should never give a girl a name derived from a river, a mountain, or a tree. Likewise, names of flowers, terrifying spirits <term>Yakshinis</term>, creepers, snakes, or names ending in the word for "gem" <term>Ratna</term> should be avoided.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

On auspicious lunar days, excluding the "Empty" days <note>Rikta tithis: the 4th, 9th, and 14th days of a lunar fortnight, considered unlucky for new beginnings</note> and Tuesdays, under movable signs and auspicious houses (4, 11, 7, 6, 10, 5, 8), and with malefic planets in houses 3, 6, or 11, one should perform the rites in an even-numbered auspicious sign.

### Placing the Child in the Cradle
On lunar days that are not "Empty" and not Tuesday, under the "Soft," "Fixed," or "Swift" constellations <note>Mridu, Dhruva, and Kshipra Nakshatras</note>, on an auspicious weekday, the child should be placed in the cradle with their head facing East while remembering Lord Vishnu. This should be done on the 10th, 12th, 16th, or 22nd day after birth for boys, or the 12th or 13th day for girls.

### Drinking Milk (Weaning)
Under the constellations Uttara Phalguni, Hasta, Chitra, Shravana, Dhanishta, Revati, Ashwini, Magha, Swati, Shatabhisha, Pushya, Rohini, Mrigashirsha, or Anuradha; avoiding the lunar days 6, 4, 8, 14, 15, and 30; avoiding the Vishti Karana <note>an inauspicious astrological period</note> and fixed Karanas; avoiding inauspicious planetary yogas; and avoiding the period after the 10th day of the dark fortnight—after the first month has passed, in the morning or midday, under day-strength zodiac signs. One must avoid the "mouth" of Rahu, Rudra, and the Yogini <note>celestial spirits/energies whose positions shift and can be obstructive</note>. The movement of the Yogini is considered for journeys, while Rahu and Rudra must be meditated upon via their respective charts.

# Muhurta Sindhu
### (Page 86)

Avoiding the 2nd, 8th, and 12th <term>Lagna</term><note>The rising sign or zodiacal point on the eastern horizon</note> as well as the lunar day, on an auspicious Lagna and an auspicious weekday, in an auspicious division of the sign, and with the 8th house being pure <note>free from planetary influence</note>, with benefics in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, or 9th houses and malefic planets in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th: the child should be bathed and have the <term>Svastyayana</term><note>a ritual for invoking well-being</note> performed. Then, the child should be taken to a temple, where the deity is worshipped, and then taken to the house of the maternal uncle or others.

**The Binding of the Loincloth**
In the bright fortnight, under the <term>Nakshatras</term><note>Lunar mansions or star clusters</note> of Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Vishakha, Anuradha, the three Uttaras, Rohini, Pushya, Ashwini, Magha, or Revati, on an auspicious weekday and a virtuous lunar day.

**Sitting on the Ground and Binding the Waist-Thread**
Having worshipped the Earth and the Boar incarnation <note>Varaha, who lifted the earth from the ocean</note>, when Mars is strong in the fifth month, under the Nakshatras of Shravana, Rohini, Mrigashira, Jyeshtha, Anuradha, Ashwini, Tishya, or Abhijit, on a lunar day other than the <term>Rikta</term><note>"Empty" days: the 4th, 9th, and 14th of the lunar month</note> days, on an auspicious weekday and in a fixed Lagna, one should bind small bells <insert>Kshudra-ghantika</insert> around the child and place them on the ground. The prayer is:

> O Goddess Earth, protect this child, who is always auspicious and omnipresent.
> O Beloved of Shiva, bestow upon them full life and vital breath.

One should place these items in front of the child: cloth, a weapon, a pen, a book, gold, and silver. Whichever item the child grasps first shall indicate their future livelihood.

**The First Feeding of Solid Food**
For boys, this should be done in even months starting from the sixth month. For girls, it should be done in odd months starting from the fifth month. It should be performed under the Nakshatras of Mrigashira, Revati, Chitra, Anuradha, Hasta, Ashwini, Tishya, Abhijit, Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, the three Uttaras, or Rohini. On the 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 10th, 13th, or 15th lunar days, on an auspicious weekday. The Lagnas of Pisces and Aries should be avoided. The Lagna should be different from the 8th house relative to the birth Lagna and birth sign. Benefics should be in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 5th, or 9th houses, and malefics in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th. The 10th house should be pure and the Moon should not be in the 6th or 8th. Some say the birth Nakshatra is auspicious for this. For the <term>Samskaras</term><note>Sacred life-cycle rituals</note> starting from conception through the first feeding of the child, there is no fault caused by the combustion of Jupiter or Venus or the intercalary month <note>Malmasa</note>.

**Specifics of the Food**
Know that eating on the birth Nakshatra causes a loss of prosperity, while eating on the <term>Karma</term> Nakshatra <note>The 10th star from the birth star</note> brings happiness. Eating on the <term>Adhana</term> Nakshatra <note>The 19th star from the birth star</note> destroys diseases for children. One who eats sweet food lives...

# The Ocean of Auspicious Times

If the ceremony is performed on a Friday, the person becomes eloquent; on a Sunday, they become poor; on a Tuesday, they suffer from disease; on a Wednesday, they become a "bhogi" <note>one who enjoys worldly pleasures and comforts</note>; and on a Saturday, their lifespan is diminished. However, the days of the Sun, Mars, and Saturn <note>Sunday, Tuesday, and Saturday, usually considered harsh</note> are also auspicious if the lord of that day is situated in its sign of exaltation or a friend's house, or is aspected by Jupiter. The days and divisions of Jupiter, Mercury, Venus, and the Moon are generally excellent. The signs of the Moon, Sun, and Saturn are inauspicious. The signs 2, 11, 7, 6, 5, 4, and 10 <note>Taurus, Aquarius, Libra, Virgo, Leo, Cancer, and Capricorn</note> are auspicious. 1 and 8 <note>Aries and Scorpio</note> should be avoided. Benefic planets should be in the centers or trines <note>houses 1, 4, 7, 10 or 1, 5, 9</note>, while malefic planets should be in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses. The Moon is not auspicious in the 12th, 6th, or 8th houses. If the Moon is in the sign of its debilitation at the time of the rising sign <term>Lagna</term>, it is censurable. If the Sun is in the rising sign, the person may suffer from skin diseases; if Mars, they suffer from bile-related illnesses; if Saturn, they suffer from wind-related <note>Vata</note> disorders; if the Moon is weak, they become a beggar. If Mercury is present, they become wise and enjoy life; if Venus, they have a long life; if Jupiter, or a full Moon, the person becomes a performer of sacrifices <note>Yajva</note>. Regarding the first feeding of grains <note>Annaprashana</note>, some authorities say the 12th, 9th, 8th, 10th, 5th, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses should be considered. The combination of the Anuradha star, Sunday, and the 6th lunar day is widely considered censurable.

## On the Consumption of Betel Leaves

The auspicious stars are the three Uttaras, Rohini, Mrigashirsha, Revati, Chitra, Anuradha, Hasta, Ashwini, Pushya, Abhijit, Shravana, Mrigashirsha, Punarvasu, Jyeshtha, Swati, and Dhanishtha. The rising signs should be 3, 6, 9, 10, 11, or 12 <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, or Pisces</note>. It should be on the days of benefic planets. Benefics should be in 1, 4, 7, 10, 9, or 5, and malefics in 3 or 6. This is the timing for the first feeding of solids <note>Annashana</note> at two and a half months.

## On the Piercing of the Ears

This should be done on the 12th or 16th day after birth, or in the 6th, 7th, or 8th month, or in an odd-numbered year. Avoid the months of Chaitra and Pausha, and the four months of the rainy season <note>Chaturmasya</note>. Avoid the birth month, the "empty" lunar days <note>Rikta tithis: 4, 9, 14</note>, the 8th day, the new moon, and "lost" days <note>Avama</note>. Avoid the birth stars 1, 10, and 16. The auspicious stars are Shravana, Dhanishtha, Punarvasu, Mrigashirsha, Revati, Chitra, Anuradha, Hasta, Ashwini, Pushya, and Abhijit. It should be a benefic day with the 8th house being pure. Benefics should be in 1, 4, 7, 10, 9, or 5, and malefics in 3, 6, or 11. Ear-piercing is auspicious in the rising signs 2, 7, 9, or 12 when joined by Jupiter. A golden needle should be used for a prince, silver for a Brahmin or Vaishya, and an iron needle for a Shudra.

One should pierce the ears of a woman or a man—the left and right respectively—using a needle eight finger-widths long, in a pleasant, clean, and beautiful location on the ground. Regarding this, there are specific rules:

**Garga** states: The months of Kartika, Pausha, Chaitra, or Phalguna are praised for ear-piercing <term>Karnavedha: the ritual piercing of the ears</term>, specifically during the bright fortnight on an auspicious day. One should avoid the 11th and 8th lunar days, the "empty" days <note>Rikta tithis: 4th, 9th, and 14th</note>, and the transition days <note>Parva</note>. One must also avoid the Shakuni period and the Vishti <note>inauspicious astrological timing</note>.

**Vriddha Narada** says: Ear-piercing should be done when the sun or ascendant is in Taurus, Gemini, Pisces, Cancer, Virgo, Libra, or Sagittarius. Aries and Capricorn are mediocre; Leo, Scorpio, and Aquarius are the worst.
Jupiter in the 8th, 6th, or 12th house; Mercury in the 5th or 8th; Venus in the 7th or 8th—these positions are to be avoided. The Moon is auspicious in the 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th, or 10th houses.

### On the Piercing of a Maiden's Nose
The nose-piercing <term>Ghranavedha</term> follows the same stars as ear-piercing, specifically the three "Uttara" stars, Shatabhisha, and Swati. It should be done in the bright fortnight, in the forenoon, on an auspicious day and lunar date.

### On Beginning Education at the Completion of a Year
This should be performed at the end of the lunar or solar year on an auspicious day, avoiding the Bhadra period, and starting on an auspicious weekday.

### On the Completion of the Year
This may follow either the solar or lunar calendar. On this occasion, worship should be performed as prescribed in the ritual manuals.

### On the First Haircut
The tonsure ceremony <term>Chaulm or Chudakarana</term> should be performed in the third year, or an odd-numbered year. Some say it can be done in the first year. For all twice-born classes <note>Dvija: Brahmins, Kshatriyas, and Vaishyas</note>, this is a religious duty to be performed in the first or third year according to Vedic injunction.
Auspicious stars: Jyeshtha, Mrigashira, Revati, Chitra, Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, Hasta, and Pushya <note>The text uses abbreviations: Jye., Mri., Re., Chi., Swa., Pu., Shra., Dha., Sha., Ha.</note>.
Auspicious lunar days: 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 10th, 11th, and 15th.
It should be done on "gentle" weekdays <note>Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday</note> with gentle planets in the ascendant or the ninth division <term>Navamsha</term>. The sign should not be the 8th from the birth sign or birth ascendant. If the 8th house is purified, even Venus in the 8th is auspicious. It should be done during the Sun's northern course <term>Uttarayana</term>, excluding the month of Chaitra and transition days. One should judge the results based on planets in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses from the ascendant or in the center houses <term>Kendras</term>.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

The first haircutting ceremony <note>Sanskrit: Chaula</note> of a son should be avoided if the mother is menstruating. As stated by the sage Prachetas: "If a mother is in her menses during an auspicious rite, it leads to death, except after the fifth day." Some authorities say this rite should not be performed for the eldest child in the month of Jyeshtha <note>the third month of the Hindu lunar calendar, roughly May-June</note>. Shaving is also forbidden in one's birth month. It is said: "He who, out of delusion, undergoes shaving, starts a journey, or pierces his ears in his birth month, will surely suffer disease and the loss of wealth and sons." He may even face death or imprisonment. Here are the specific details:

If the Sun is in the 7th house during the 4th, 6th, 7th, 10th, or 12th Ascendants <note>Lagna</note>, it brings death. Mars or Venus in these positions brings happiness, but Saturn brings destruction and misfortune. If Mercury, Venus, or a strong Jupiter are in the trines or angles <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, it is an excellent yoga <note>alignment</note> for the haircutting ceremony. Another favorable alignment occurs when Venus is in the 12th, the Ascendant is in the 10th, the Sun is present, and Jupiter is in an angle. Alternatively, if Mercury and Venus are in Cancer or Leo, and the Sun is in Taurus or Gemini, it is auspicious. Another yoga: Sun in the 11th, Mercury in the 12th, Venus in the 1st, and the Moon in an angle. Even if planets are in unfavorable signs, if they are in auspicious subdivisions <note>Amshas</note> and aspected by Jupiter, they become beneficial.

### General Rules for Shaving
The days and lunar mansions <note>Nakshatras</note> mentioned for the first haircutting also apply to general shaving <note>Kshaura</note>. Shaving should not be done on the ninth day from a previous shaving, during twilight, on "empty" lunar days <note>Rikta tithis: 4th, 9th, 14th</note>, on full/new moon days <note>Parva</note>, at night, while breathing heavily, or after eating and anointing with oil. However, one may shave during a sacrifice <note>Yajna</note>, a wedding, upon the death of parents, upon release from prison, or by the command of a King or a Priest.

The lunar mansions Magha, Anuradha, Rohini, the three Uttaras, and Krittika are considered "life-taking" and should be avoided for shaving, as should Sundays, Tuesdays, and Saturdays. Even if the lunar mansion is unfavorable, one may shave on Wednesdays or Mondays. However, even then, one should avoid the mansions Mula and Anuradha. If the Moon and the birth star <note>Tara</note> are not purified, one should still prefer Wednesday or Monday.

Regarding the effects of the days: Shaving on a Thursday destroys life; on a Friday, it destroys virility; on a Sunday, it destroys wealth; on a Tuesday, it destroys longevity; and on a Saturday, it destroys everything. For those employed in royal service <note>government officials</note> or those who live by their appearance <note>actors or professionals</note>, there is no strict requirement to examine the astrological timing for trimming the beard, body hair, or nails.

The six stars of Krittika, the five of Magha, the three of Anuradha <note>original: "maitra"</note>, the eight of Rohini <note>original: "brahma"</note>, and the four of the Uttara group are auspicious for shaving. It is a clear tradition that even the four-faced creator Brahma cannot count the merits of shaving during these times. **Now, regarding the shaving ritual for kings:** For kings, the trimming of the beard is prescribed on the fifth day under a shaving-star. If a shaving-star is not available on the fifth day, the ritual should be performed during the specific hour <term>Muhurta: a unit of time approximately 48 minutes long</term> ruled by the lord of that star. **Now, regarding the shaving ritual for ascetics and others:** For ascetics <term>Sannyasis: those who have renounced worldly life</term>, shaving is done on the Full Moon and New Moon days; for widows, it is permitted always. However, the consideration of purity and other factors must not be neglected. **Now, the beginning of education <term>Akshara-arambha: the ritual of first writing letters</term>:** This should occur during the northern transit of the sun <term>Uttarayana: the six-month period when the sun moves north, considered spiritually auspicious</term> in the child's fifth year. After bowing to and worshipping Ganesha, Saraswati <note>the goddess of learning</note>, and the family deity, the ritual should be held under the stars of Hasta, Pushya, Swati, Anuradha, Jyeshtha, Revati, Ashwini, or Chitra. It should be on a Friday, Thursday, or Wednesday, on auspicious lunar days (2nd, 3rd, 5th, 11th, or 12th). It is auspicious in the bright fortnight, provided the Moon is not in the eighth house of the birth chart, and avoiding the month when the Sun is in Aquarius. Now follows the chart starting from the Sun's position. **Now, the offering of auspicious sprouts:** This should be done when the Moon and stars are pure on an auspicious day and lunar date.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments
<note>original: "Muhurta Sindhu"</note>

The positions 6, 3, and 11 are worshipful <note>favorable</note>; 4, 8, and 12 are censured <note>unfavorable</note>. The strength of Time is even more powerful than the strength of Jupiter. For a young boy's initiation <term>Upanayana: the sacred thread ceremony marking the start of student life</term> and also for marriage, the strength of the Sun is considered: positions 3, 6, 10, and 11 are excellent; 1, 2, 5, 7, and 8 are worshipful; 4, 8, and 12 are censured. Positions 2, 5, and 8 become auspicious after thirteen days. In the Northern Transit of the Sun <term>Uttarayana: the period between the winter and summer solstices</term>, until the tenth day of the bright half of the month of Ashadha, the initiation is praised even if Jupiter is weak, provided the Sun is in the sign of Pisces during the month of Chaitra. If a boy has reached his eighth year and no other purification of time is found, his initiation is auspicious when the Sun is in Pisces during Chaitra. If purification is not found through the transit of planets or the eight-fold division of the zodiac <term>Ashtakavarga: a system of calculating planetary strength</term>, then the initiation should be performed while the Sun is in Pisces in the month of Chaitra.

The "Throat-Seizing" days <note>Galagraha: specific lunar days forbidden for starting Vedic study</note> are prohibited by Jupiter. One initiated during the evening twilight <term>Pradosha</term>, at night, on a non-study day <term>Anadhyaya</term>, or during a "Throat-Seizing" day—unless it is during the month of Madhu <note>Chaitra</note>—deserves to have the sacrament performed again. The evening twilight restriction applies in all months to the 3rd, 6th, and 12th lunar days respectively for 1, 1.5, and 2 quarters of the night <note>a quarter of the night is roughly 3 hours</note> after the entry of the 4th, 7th, and 13th lunar days.

The non-study days are: Ashadha bright 10th, Jyeshtha 2nd, Ashadha bright 11th, Magha bright 12th, as well as the 14th, 15th (Full Moon), 30th (New Moon), 1st, and 8th lunar days. Also, during a solar transit <term>Sankranti</term> and when the moon is in the Punarvasu constellation, a Brahmin's vow should not be taken, according to the saying "not in Punarvasu." In the vow of initiation, the "Arrow of Disease" <note>Rogabana: a specific inauspicious astrological calculation</note> is also censured.

### Results of the Months for Initiation
In the month of Magha, one becomes very wealthy. In Phalguna, a lord of wealth, wise, and strong. In Chaitra, one becomes endowed with the Vedas. In Vaishakha, fortunate, happy, and a leader. In Jyeshtha, an eminent scholar. In Ashadha, a conqueror of great opponents and a famous great Pandit.

### Results of the Days of the Week
On Sunday, one becomes intelligent; on Monday, clever; on Wednesday, enlightened. On Tuesday and Saturday, one meets an early death <note>literally "five-ness," referring to the five elements dissolving</note>. On Friday, one becomes eloquent, strong, and pure. On Thursday, one is devoted to the six duties <note>the traditional duties of a Brahmin</note>, happy, learned, and long-lived. If the birth star is afflicted by malefic planets, even if a planet is in its exaltation or is combust, the person may have a short life.

Therefore, because of the influence of the planets and the nature of Time...

# The Ocean of Auspicious Times

<page-num>92</page-num>
->The Ocean of Auspicious Times<-

Peace offerings to the planets should be performed, but not for the entire year. When the time for a religious vow <note>vrata</note> has arrived and a person lacks astrological purity, they should perform a penance according to their ability and then proceed with the **Sacred Thread Ceremony** <term>Mauñjibandhana: the investiture of the sacred thread</term>. For the twice-born classes, the autumn, summer, and spring seasons are recommended in reverse order of preference. The five months starting from the month of *Tapas* <note>the month of Magha, Jan-Feb</note> are generally the most important. In the month of Jyeshtha <note>May-June</note>, one should specifically avoid the ceremony for an eldest son, as it may lead to dullness of intellect or even death. One should avoid the birth month for both marriage and the sacred thread ceremony. Vasistha and other sages specifically emphasize avoiding the birth fortnight. Vasistha condemns the actual birthday; Garga condemns the ten days following it; and Bhaguri condemns the entire birth fortnight. Others, however, consider the birth month to be praiseworthy. Even where the birth month is forbidden, one should at least avoid the ten days starting from the birthday; the dates following those are auspicious. Regarding the statements that the dark fortnight is excellent, those refer only to a second initiation <note>a renewal of the vow</note>. On the day before or the day after a "non-study" day <term>Anadhyaya: days when Vedic recitation is forbidden</term>, one should not perform the thread ceremony, the conclusion of studies, or the beginning of education.

**The division of this rule is as follows:**
The time before the ceremony is unfavorable for students of the *Yajur Veda*; the day itself is unfavorable for students of the *Sama Veda*; and the day after is unfavorable for students of the *Atharva Veda*. On the *Ashtaka* days, the *Sarga* days, and the beginnings of the *Yugas* and *Manvantaras*, one should observe the non-study rule, as well as on the *Soyapada* days. The *Soyapada* days are known as: the two Solstices, the two Equinoxes, the second day of the bright half of Jyeshtha, the tenth day of the bright half of Ashvina, and the fourth and twelfth days of Magha. As the sage Garga said of old: "One may perform a rite even on a non-study day if it is an occasional necessity." The seventh day of the bright half of Magha, the third day of the bright half of Vaishakha <note>Akshaya Tritiya</note>, and the third day of the dark half of Phalguna are auspicious for the sacred thread ceremony. Likewise, the first day of the dark fortnight is suitable for an initiation performed as a general penance. The days starting from the first of the dark fortnight are considered "divested of Vedic study" and are intended for penance-related initiations.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Times

<page-num>93</page-num>

->**The Binding of the Girdle**<-

Regarding the binding of the girdle <note>original: "mekhalā-bandhana"; the ceremonial tying of a triple cord around the waist of the student</note>, it is stated that one should not perform auspicious acts on the birth star <note>Janma-nakshatra</note> or on the 10th, 16th, 18th, 23rd, or 25th stars from the birth star. 

The teachers state that the days of Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus are excellent. The days of the Moon and the Sun provide middling results, while the other days <note>Tuesday and Saturday</note> are condemned for this vow. For all classes, the days of Jupiter and Mercury are recommended for the vow. For the Brahmin and Kshatriya <note>priestly and warrior classes</note>, the Moon and Sun are middling, while Tuesday is avoided. The day of Mercury should be avoided by the twice-born <note>Dvija</note> if Mercury is in combustion <note>too close to the sun to be visible</note>. The day of the waning Moon should also be avoided.

### The Lunar Mansions (Nakshatras)
The following stars are favorable: Ashvini, Hasta, Pushya, Abhijit, the three Uttaras, Rohini, Ashlesha, Svati, Punarvasu, Anuradha, Dhanishtha, Shatabhisha, Mula, Mrigashirsha, Revati, Vishakha, and Purva-Phalguni. In some traditions, Jyeshtha is also accepted. 

On the days of the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, and Venus, the day of Mercury is avoided if he is combust. The 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 10th, 11th, and 12th lunar days <note>Tithis</note> are auspicious; some say the 6th is also good in the bright fortnight. In the dark fortnight, only up to the 5th day is acceptable. 

Dividing the day into three parts: the first part is for Vedic rituals, the second for human affairs, and the third for ancestral rites <note>Pitru-karma</note>.

### Purification of the Ascendant (Lagna-shuddhi)
When Venus, Jupiter, or the Moon are in the Ascendant, it is favorable. Saturn in the 6th or 8th house is not auspicious. The Moon and Venus in the 12th house from the Ascendant do not grant good results. Malefic planets in the 1st, 5th, or 8th houses are not auspicious. Benefics in the 6th, 8th, or 12th are not good, while malefics in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses grant good results. A full Moon in Taurus or Cancer in the Ascendant is best; otherwise, it is not. 

In whatever sign the Moon is placed, if it is in a favorable ninth-division <note>Navamsha</note>, the initiate will be devoted to learning. If the Moon is in a malefic division, he will be poor. If it is in the Cancer division, he will suffer grief. However, if the Moon is in Shravana or Pushya stars while in the Cancer division, he will become wealthy.

One must also observe the "Seven-Spear Chart" <note>Sapta-shalaka Chakra; a complex diagram used to detect "vedha" or planetary obstructions</note> to check for obstructions. The strength of the Lord of the Veda, the Lord of the Day, and the Lord of the Ascendant must be considered. The strength of the Lord of the specific Vedic branch <note>Shakha-adhipati</note> is vital. The day of the branch-lord and the ascendant of the branch-lord are difficult to obtain simultaneously. When these three are aligned with the strength of the Lord of the boy's Varna <note>social class</note>, the initiation ceremony <note>Upanayana</note> is beneficial for all.

When the Sun and Moon are powerful, and Jupiter and Venus are not in an enemy's house, nor defeated in planetary war, nor in debilitation, a man should perform the rites. Otherwise, he remains devoid of the fruits of the Vedic scriptures.

**The Binding of the Royal Scepter:** This should be done in the months and lunar days prescribed for religious vows, excluding the month of Chaitra <note>March-April</note>, and when Mars is not combust.

**Regarding the First Shaving (Keshanta) and Returning Home from Study (Samavartana):** The first shaving of the beard should be performed in the sixteenth year on a day auspicious for the tonsure ceremony.

The *Samavartana* <note>the graduation ceremony marking the end of student life</note> is desired on the days prescribed for religious vows.

**Further Special Rules:** From the time of an earthquake, or from the time of a meteor strike, or the appearance of a comet in the sky, the wise say that religious vows and ceremonies are obstructed. If a comet appears in the first part of the sky, the ritual acts performed then are remembered as being as fruitless as if they had never happened. This applies for a period of three months. 

The sage Garga says: In the event of eclipses, earthquakes, comets, or falling meteors, the experts say the defect lasts for ten days; some say thirteen days. Chandeshwara states: In the event of a fire in the directions <note>unusual atmospheric glows</note>, an earthquake, a lightning strike, or the appearance of a comet or falling meteor, the defect must be observed.

All planets are auspicious in the 11th house of gains. Venus, the Moon, and the Lord of the Ascendant are beneficial in the 6th house for the thread ceremony, education, and good works. If the Sun is strong in the Ascendant, it is also auspicious. The Sun in the 10th house is similarly beneficial. The Sun is the lord of all branches of knowledge for everyone during the binding of the vow <note>Upanayana/Thread Ceremony</note>. However, the Moon is forbidden in the Ascendant even if it is in its sign of exaltation. 

**Narada** states: "If the cold-rayed one <note>the Moon</note> is in the Ascendant, even if exalted, it makes the initiate constantly poor and suffering from wasting diseases." **Brihaspati** says: "In the bright fortnight, if the Moon is in its own sign or exalted, it is particularly auspicious." In case of conflict between these two views, the statement of Brihaspati is more appropriate as it is accepted by many authorities. If the Sun is in a cardinal house <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th</note>, it destroys the lineage of the initiate. If Mars is there, it destroys the student and the teacher. If Saturn is there, it brings various diseases. Rahu causes loss of wealth, as does Ketu. At the auspicious moment, the initiation into the Gayatri mantra is praised; that indeed is the beginning of the divine path.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

During the bright fortnight <note>the waxing phase of the moon</note>, when the purifications prescribed for vows are met, and the eighth house is pure <note>free of planets</note> at the time of sunrise, on the 2nd, 5th, 6th, 7th, 9th, or 10th lunar days. With benefics in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, one should perform the ceremony. ### Regarding the Commencement of Education
During the Northern Transit of the Sun <note>Uttarayana, the six-month period after the winter solstice</note>, in the month of Ashvina, when Mercury is strong, one should first worship Lord Ganesha and Goddess Saraswati <note>the deities of wisdom and learning</note>. The auspicious lunar mansions <note>Nakshatras</note> are: Hasta, Chitra, Swati, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Purva Bhadrapada, Uttara Bhadrapada, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Mrigashira, Ardra, Punarvasu, Pushya, Ashlesha, Mula, Ashwini, Revati, and Anuradha. 

In the bright fortnight, on the 2nd, 3rd, 5th, 6th, 10th, 11th, or 12th lunar days (or the 7th and 13th). In the dark fortnight, only the first third of the phase is acceptable. One must avoid the "non-reading days" <note>Anadhyaya; traditional holidays when Vedic study is forbidden</note> and festival days. The preferred days are Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday. One should avoid the Sun and Mars in the Ascendant <note>Lagna</note>. 

Dual-natured signs <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note> are preferred for the Ascendant. Malefics should be in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, while benefics should occupy the 1st, 4, 7th, or 10th houses. The 5th house must be free of malefic planets and the 8th house must be pure. In a movable Ascendant, the student may wander; in a fixed Ascendant, there may be dullness or stagnation. Thus, the commencement of all learning must be carefully timed. 

The days immediately preceding and following a "non-reading day" should also be avoided according to some authorities. Evening time is generally considered censurable for starting studies. 

**Special Combinations for Learning:**
* **Wednesday:** If the Ascendant is the 3rd or 6th sign <note>Gemini or Virgo</note>, or in the hour <note>Hora</note> or subdivision <note>Amsha</note> of Mercury.
* **Monday:** When the Moon is in the mansion of Hasta, in a subdivision of Mercury, in a movable Ascendant, and joined by the Sun, Moon, and Mercury.
* **Wednesday (Advanced):** When the Moon is in Hasta, in the hour of Mercury, and Mercury is in its own subdivision or in a dual-natured Ascendant.
* **Virgo Ascendant:** When Mercury is at its highest exaltation point, joined with the Sun on a Wednesday.
* **Sunday/Monday:** When the Moon is in Mrigashira or Hasta, with Cancer or Leo as the Ascendant, and in a subdivision of Mercury. 
* **General:** When Mercury is in its best divisional sign <note>Vargottama</note>, or in a subdivision of Jupiter, and Mercury, the Sun, and Venus are in the center houses <note>Kendras</note> on the 13th lunar day or 12th Ascendant.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments
<note>original: "Muhurtasindhu"</note>

The beginning of a mantra <note>a sacred chant or prayer</note> should occur on a day other than a Vyatireka <note>an inauspicious astrological yoga</note>. One should begin the mantra of a specific deity on the day associated with that deity's gateway. The constellations <note>Nakshatras</note> recommended are the "dreadful" ones: Ardra, Ashlesha, Jyeshtha, and Mula <note>original: "ā · ti · jye ·"</note>, as well as Shravana, Swati, Vishakha, the three Uttaras, Rohini, and others. The auspicious lunar days <note>Tithis</note> are the 6th, 13th, 5th, 10th, 15th, 2nd, 7th, and 12th. The preferred days of the week are Thursday, Wednesday, and Sunday, though some authorities also accept Friday.

**Regarding the commencement of Jain religious duties:** Use the constellations Uttarashadha, Ashvini, Mrigashira, Swati, Pushya, and Chitra. Perform these on the "Jaya" <note>3rd, 8th, 13th</note> or "Purna" <note>5th, 10th, 15th</note> lunar days, on Tuesday, Wednesday, or Friday, under an auspicious rising sign <note>Lagna</note>.

**Regarding the ritual reading of texts:** Use constellations other than the "dreadful" or "fierce" ones. Avoid Saturdays and the "neck-choking" <note>Galagraha</note> days. It should be done when the moon is in a human sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Libra, or Aquarius</note> in the 5th or 9th house.

**Regarding the hearing of the Puranas <note>ancient chronicles</note>:** Avoid the "empty" <note>Rikta</note> lunar days and Tuesdays or Saturdays. Use the "soft," "fixed," "swift," or "movable" constellations. It should be done in a movable rising sign with auspicious planets in the center houses. For the Ramayana, the reading should be completed within the first ten "ghatikas" <note>approx. 4 hours</note> of the morning.

**Regarding Marriage:** Based on the teaching that "one should not remain without an ashrama <note>stage of life</note>," after completing one's studies and giving a gift to the teacher, one should become a householder with the teacher's permission. First, seek a groom who possesses virility, comes from a noble family, is virtuous, and strong. Then, after honoring the astrologer with flowers, fruit, and gold, examine the marriage prospects. Success in marriage is found under an auspicious rising sign and favorable omens. If the lord of the 12th house is in the 1st, or the lord of the 1st is in the 12th, a marriage occurs. If the moon is in a fixed sign and not afflicted by malefic planets, and is aspected by Jupiter in the 3rd, 5th, 7th, 11th, or 10th house, it is favorable. If the Moon and the Lord of the 1st house are in the 7th house, a bride is obtained. If the Lord of the 7th and the Moon are in the 1st or 12th house, a groom is obtained.

# Ocean of Auspicious Moments

If the seventh house is associated with or aspected by Venus, a bride will be obtained. If the seventh house is aspected by or associated with both the Moon and Venus, the acquisition of a bride is certain. If any one of the following—the waning Moon, Mars, Saturn, or the Sun—is in the Ascendant, it leads to death. If a malefic planet is in the seventh house, the groom dies within five years. If the Sun is in the seventh house, the offspring will be stillborn. If a malefic is in the Ascendant, the woman may be unchaste. If a malefic is in the seventh, death occurs in seven years; if Saturn and Mars are there, death occurs in seven months. Jupiter and Mercury in the seventh grant long life, five sons, and wealth in cattle. If the Moon is in the sixth or eighth house from the Ascendant, death occurs within a year. If a malefic is in the Ascendant and Mars is in the seventh, the woman becomes a widow in eight years. If the seventh house from the Ascendant contains a malefic planet that is aspected by an enemy or is in its sign of debilitation, the woman will have deceased children or be of ill-repute.

A marriage performed is excellent, middling, or inferior in that order. Marriage in the same zodiac sign is auspicious, but the same lunar mansion <insert>within that sign</insert> brings loss of memory <note>or loss of tradition/legacy</note>. If the lunar mansions are different, it is auspicious; so says the sage Shaunaka. The Pulse <term>Nadi: representing the physiological/energetic temperament</term> and Temperament <term>Gana</term> should be considered when the signs are the same but the mansions differ. 

Regarding Krittika and Kumbha <note>Pleiades and Aquarius</note>, or the two Vishakhas, or Swati, or Purva Bhadrapada and Shatabhisha: if they are in the same sign but different mansions, and the man's star comes first, it is said to be exceedingly beautiful <note>highly auspicious</insert>. If the woman's star comes first, it leads to destruction. 

The auspicious stars are: Rohini, Ardra, Magha, Jyeshtha, Krittika, Pushya, Mrigashira, Revati, and Uttara Bhadrapada. In the same sign, if the couple has the same lunar mansion but different quarters <note>Padas</note>, it brings prosperity. However, if the couple shares the same quarter of a mansion, death is certain within three years. 

Great affection arises from being in the same sign. The fourth and tenth positions are auspicious; the third and eleventh bring wealth; the seventh position <note>directly opposite</note> brings good offspring. The seventh position is particularly auspicious for Aquarius and Leo when joining hands in marriage. However, for Capricorn and Cancer, or Aquarius and Leo <insert>in certain contexts</insert>, the mutual seventh position may indicate early widowhood; one must be careful. 

In the combinations of Pisces-Scorpio, Aquarius-Gemini, or Capricorn-Virgo, one should not perform the marriage in the five-nine relationship <note>Navapanchama</note>. If the signs are even, they are equal; if odd, they are associated with the eighth or twelfth positions. This is not desired in reverse, though a strong Leo is acceptable. 

If the lords of the signs are friendly, the defect is small. Even in the two-twelve relationship, there is no defect if the divisional signs <note>Amshakas</note> are compatible. The 'Pulse' <note>Nadi</note> defect: the initial pulse kills the husband, the final pulse kills the bride, and the middle pulse kills both. Therefore, one must avoid <insert>matching</insert> the same Nadi.

A direct obstruction <term>Vedha: an astrological interference between planets or stars</term> acts quickly, while a distant obstruction takes time. If an obstruction begins during the transition between stars, a year of misfortune befalls the subjects. If both partners fall within the first "pulse" <term>Nadi: one of the three physiological/energetic temperaments in Vedic astrology</term>, it leads to poverty. If both are in the middle pulse, it leads to destruction. If both are in the final pulse, it leads to good fortune.

Regarding the calculation of these pulses for a maiden, starting from the star Krittika: in the Jangala <note>arid/wild</note> regions, a four-fold garland <note>system of four Nadis</note> is used; in the Panchala region, a five-fold garland is used; and in other regions, a three-fold garland is favored by the sages for marriage. To understand the four-pulse and five-pulse systems, they are arranged in the following charts:

Shaunaka says: If the planetary friendship is favorable, it grants the desired results. Even if there is enmity between the phonetic groups <note>Vargas</note> or the temperamental categories <note>Ganas</note>, which usually causes hardship for the couple, all such "bad Kuta" <note>faults in the matching system</note> are destroyed if there is friendship between the lords of the planets. Narada says: Regarding the distance between the birth stars <note>Nakshatras</note> of the bride and groom: if the groom's star is within the first nine stars from the bride's, it is considered "distant" and is condemned. In the second set of nine, it is considered middling, and in the third set of nine, it is favorable. Now, regarding the phonetic groups <note>Vargas</note>: the fifth group from one's own is an enemy, the fourth is a friend, and others are neutral.

Regarding the 6th and 8th positions <note>Shashtashtaka - a difficult astrological alignment</note>: if this occurs, one should donate a cow and a bull. For the 9th and 5th positions, one should give bronze and silver, as well as cloth, gold, and a horse. In other cases, one should satisfy the priests <note>Brahmins</note> with offerings. These prohibitions are removed by performing the prescribed donations; then the marriage may proceed under favorable omens. 

### Exceptions to Compatibility Rules
In cases where a bride is won in battle, obtained through a treaty, given out of affection, or comes of her own accord, one need not examine the purity of the astrological matching <note>Melaka</note>. When many daughters are born to the same parents, the matching should be calculated for the eldest; for the younger ones, it need not be considered. 

<note>Note: This applies to giving multiple daughters to different grooms, not two daughters to the same man, as that is forbidden.</note> 

Two daughters should not be given to the same man. In "Asura" <note>marriage by purchase</note> and other such marriage rites, the "Rashikuta" <note>zodiac compatibility</note> need not be considered. This also applies to those with physical disabilities, the very elderly, the unfortunate, or those remarrying <note>Punarbhu</note>.

### Evaluation of Points
Regarding the calculation of points <note>Gunas</note>: 16 points are considered poor/reproachable, 20 are middling, and 30 points are excellent; anything beyond that is the highest/best. According to the "Saddakuta": 20 points are poor, 25 are middling, 30 are excellent, and beyond that is superior. Having thus understood the qualities, one should proceed with the determination of the marriage.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

Under the constellations of Rohini, Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada, Swati, Vishakha, Dhanishta, Ashwini, and Shravana; on an auspicious day of the week, in the presence of others, and during a favorable planetary alignment; with the strength of the Moon and in the presence of the sacred fire; the father of the bride—addressing the groom who is bathed, adorned with flowers, and free from disease—shall say: "I shall give this girl to you, provided you are not a fallen man and are free from all defects. I give this girl to you in the presence of the Twice-born <note>referring to Brahmins</note>, the Gods, and the Fire." To you, who seeks a bride, he offers the <term>Kanyadana</term> <note>the ritual gift of a daughter in marriage</note> by word of mouth. ### || Now, the Selection of the Bride ||

On a day when the five limbs of the calendar <note>Panchanga</note> are pure and the Moon and stars are strong; specifically under the constellations of Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada, Purva Phalguni, Purva Ashadha, Purva Bhadrapada, Shravana, Dhanishta, Revati, and Anuradha; on an auspicious day and lunar date, one should select the maiden while facing West. During a favorable rising sign <note>Lagna</note>, with benefics in the 5th, 8th, 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses, and malefic planets in the 6th, 3rd, and 11th houses (the houses of improvement), one should worship Jupiter and Indrani <note>the goddess Shachi</note>. The groom or the groom’s priest should then give clothing, ornaments, and the <term>Saubhagyashtaka</term> <note>eight auspicious items signifying good fortune</note> to the maiden.

### || Now, the Selection of the Groom ||

On an auspicious day under the constellations of the three Uttaras, Krittika, Rohini, and Purva Phalguni; on a favorable day of the week, in the presence of witnesses and during an auspicious alignment; the bride’s brother or the priest should honor the groom with the sacred thread and other gifts. The <term>Saubhagyashtaka</term> should be tied in the garments of both parties. These eight items of good fortune are: 1. Turmeric, 2. Honey and Ghee, 3. Jaggery, 4. Milk, 5. Rice grains, 6. Coriander, 7. A ring, and 8. Gunja seeds.

### || Now, the Decision on the Time of Marriage ||

For girls, marriage is auspicious in even-numbered years after the age of menstruation, depending on the purity of Jupiter. For men, marriage is auspicious in odd-numbered years when purity is established. For both the bride and groom, the marriage should occur when the Moon is pure. The sage Vyasa says:
> A girl of eight years is called Gauri; at nine, she is Rohini; at ten, she is Kanya; and at twelve, she is considered a Vrishali <note>one who has reached puberty</note>. If a girl has passed her tenth year and lacks the required astrological purity, her marriage is still permitted if the stars, Moon, and rising sign are favorable. If a father does not give his daughter in marriage by her twelfth year, the giver certainly drinks her menstrual blood month after month. The father, the grandfather...

## The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

The great brother, the paternal uncle, and the maternal uncle—these five go to hell upon seeing a maiden who has reached menstruation <note>original: "rajasvalām"; this refers to the traditional anxiety regarding the delay of a daughter's marriage past puberty</note>. **Narada** states: Marriage should not be performed in the birth month, on the birth star <term>Nakshatra: the lunar mansion or star sign under which one is born</term>, or on the birth day itself. This applies to the first-born son or daughter. If one is married on their birth star, they might occasionally be dear to their husband; if married during the performance of sacrificial rites, she remains constantly beloved by her husband.

Marriage in the birth month is generally considered auspicious; however, in the birth star, birth sign, or birth ascendant, it is auspicious only if the Moon is not positioned in the birth sign. If the marriage occurs on the birth star or birth ascendant, the bride will be devoted to her husband. In the birth month, she will be wealthy and blessed with many sons. If the marriage occurs on the birth star, she will certainly be wealthy and have a lasting lineage. However, the noble teachers say that performing auspicious or nourishing rites in the birth ascendant, star, or month is inauspicious during "Shruti-vedha" <note>a specific astronomical interference</note> or solar journeys.

**Guru** states: The marriage of an eldest son with an eldest daughter should not be performed. If only one of them is the eldest, the "eldest-defect" <note>original: "jyeṣṭha-doṣa"</note> still brings harm. **Varaha** says: Two "eldests" <note>e.g., eldest groom and eldest month</note> are considered mediocre; one "eldest" is auspicious; but three "eldests" <note>eldest son, eldest daughter, and the month of Jyeshtha</note> should never be combined in marriage—this is agreed upon by all. Some say that if the Sun has left the constellation of Krittika, the marriage of an eldest daughter and eldest groom can occur in the month of Jyeshtha.

**Bharadwaja**, however, prohibited even the month of Margashirsha for the eldest: One should carefully avoid the tonsure <note>shaving of the head</note>, marriage, or initiation vows for the first-born son or daughter in the months of Margashirsha and Jyeshtha. Furthermore, this is well-known among the Southerners: the marriage of an eldest daughter to an eldest son simply must not be done. If performed, it leads to their death. Within a family of three generations, a daughter's marriage is not auspicious within six months of a son's marriage. Shaving the head after a marriage is not auspicious. After an initiation, a tonsure, or the arrival of a new bride, the departure of a daughter <note>for her own marriage</note> is not desired within the same year, though it is auspicious if the Hindu New Year has passed. **Narada** says: After a son's wedding, a daughter's wedding should not occur in the same three-month period; nor should their initiation and wedding occur together.
