# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments.

<note>original: "Muhurta-Sindhu"</note>

Shaving the head <note>tonsure</note> is auspicious even after a previous shaving. Two brothers should not marry two sisters <insert>at the same time</insert>. Within six months, the marriage of two biological brothers is forbidden. Until the marriage auspiciousness is complete, ancestral rites <note>Shraddha</note> should not be performed; however, once the marriage ceremonies are concluded, they must certainly be performed. It is said: "During the Great Lunar Fortnight <note>Mahalaya</note>, at Gaya, or on the anniversary of a parent's death, a son who has recently married should not offer the funeral rice-balls <note>Pinda</note>." 

A girl should be given in marriage when the strength of Jupiter and the Goddess Gauri is present. A girl in her ninth year is called Rohini, and she should be given to a groom who is like the Sun <note>Bhaskara</note>. A girl should be given when the Moon is strong and the groom possesses physical vigor. Here, since marriage in the ninth year is sometimes criticized, how can there be a variation in the results for a girl designated as "Rohini"? It is said in response: Before the ninth year, specifically at three and a quarter years, or in the ages of four, seven, or nine, according to the strength of the planets, the marriage is favorable. In the Kali Yuga, the taking of the hand <note>marriage</note> is auspicious in the 8th or 7th years when the planets are strong. By this statement, when the planetary transits <term>Go-chara: the movement of planets through the zodiac signs</term> are pure, marriage can occur in the 5th, 8th, 7th, 6th, 10th, or 11th years. Because when the time exceeds eleven and a quarter years, the girl reaches puberty; at that time, the merits of the gift of a maiden are lost, so one should not delay the marriage. Here, in an odd-numbered year, the marriage should be after three months; in an even-numbered year, the marriage is at the end of three months.

### Regarding Planetary Transits

Those living in the Ari and Marunaka regions seek the purity of the Sun. Those in Dravida <note>South India</note>, Malwa, the South, and Andhra seek the purity of Jupiter. Those in Magadha, Sindh, and Maru seek the purity of both Venus and Jupiter. Those born on the slopes of the Himalayas and in the Kuru lands seek the purity of both the Sun and Jupiter. People of all regions seek the purity of the Moon. These considerations of planetary movements and the like are intended for the twice-born classes <note>the three upper social orders</note> and not for others. 

Here, the rising time of Venus and Jupiter is taken into account. Nevertheless, in urgent matters for kings or those performing state duties, marriages and other ceremonies may be performed even during the combustion <note>astronomical invisibility</note> of Jupiter or Venus, provided that peace-making rituals <term>Shanti: rites to neutralize ill omens</term> are performed. These peace-making rituals should be performed as prescribed in the ritual manuals.

Regarding the matching of horoscopes <note>Melaka</note>: for those whose birth details are unknown—

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

If the birth star is unknown, one should determine the zodiac sign based on the person's given name. All calculations for compatibility <note>original: "Rashikuta," a method of matching zodiac signs</note> should then be considered using that name-based sign, just as one would with a birth sign. One must distinguish between the birth star <note>Nakshatra</note> and the name-based star. If these are swapped or confused when matching a couple, it may lead to the death of the pair. This same principle applies to the relationship between a master and a servant.

If a husband's birth star is the second from the wife's birth star, it is considered inauspicious and is said to cause the destruction of the husband. In the *Yamala of Brahma* <note>An ancient tantric and astrological text</note>, it is stated: if the master's star is first and the servant's is second, the service will not be lasting; it will vanish like a bubble on the water. Similarly, regarding debts: the lender's star should be first and the borrower's second. One should never enter a debt relationship if the stars are reversed; even if driven by greed for money, the lender will likely die or never recover the funds. 

O Parvati! <note>The text frames this as a dialogue between the god Shiva and the goddess Parvati</note> The Lord of Life has stated in the *Damara Collection*: if the village's star is first and the resident's birth star is second, one should not live in that village, as it will cause the loss of both life and wealth.

### Regional Special Rules
In the region of Bhoja, marriage is forbidden when Jupiter is in Libra or Taurus. In the region of Suraja, marriage is forbidden when Venus is in Sagittarius or Pisces. However, in the regions of Vidarbha, Kambu, Kuru, and Karnataka, a marriage in the month of Phalguna or when the Sun is in Pisces is considered auspicious. In the coastal lands between the rivers Reva and Mahi, and in Mithila, the Sun in Pisces or Sagittarius is auspicious for weddings. In the regions of Andhra and Magadha, the month of Pausha or the Sun in Scorpio is auspicious.

### Auspicious Months for Marriage
**Narada says:** The months of Magha, Phalguna, Vaishakha, and Jyeshtha bring auspicious results. Kartika and Margashirsha are mediocre, while the others are condemned.

**Vyasa says:** While Magha, Phalguna, Vaishakha, and Margashirsha are good, a marriage in Jyeshtha or Ashadha may lead to a lack of fortune or be filled with obstacles. A girl married in Shravana, Pausha, Bhadrapada, Chaitra, Ashvin, or Kartika will quickly face widowhood. 

Some authorities say only Chaitra and Pausha should be avoided. **Apastamba** claims all seasons are suitable for marriage, while **Parashar** suggests all times are acceptable except for the peak of the rainy season.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments.

The autumn and the latter part of the cool season <note>original: "shishira"</note> are preferred. Here, excluding the months of Magha, Phalguna, and Ashadha <note>roughly January, February, and June/July</note>, the remaining nine months are considered the primary time. At night, however, one may perform the ceremony in all twelve months. Even in the Baudhayana Sutra <note>an ancient manual of Vedic rituals</note>, it is said that all months are suitable for marriage except for Shuchi, Tapas, and Tapasya <note>the ritual names for the months of Ashadha, Magha, and Phalguna</note>. Some authorities believe marriage is acceptable at all times. Regarding the solar path, the sage Matsya desires the northern transit <note>Uttarayan</note> to be complete. Similarly, the disciples of the sage Mandavya declared that one should avoid the spring nectar and choose the northern path. The sage Parashara states that marrying in the month of Chaitra <note>March/April</note> leads to misfortune, as does the four-month period starting with Ashadha <note>the monsoon retreat</note>; no wise men recommend those times. In the face of such contradictions between the domestic ritual texts <note>Grihya Sutras</note> and astrology <note>Jyotisha</note>, what should be done? The rules favoring months like Magha are intended for the Shudra class and others, because in astrology, the rules of the Sutras—such as "during the northern transit of the sun" and "during the waxing fortnight"—cannot be subverted. In different regions, the months of Bhadrapada, Karttika, and Ashvina are also permitted.

**Now, the Lunar Mansions <term>Nakshatras</term> for Marriage.**
<term>Rohini</term> <term>Mrigashira</term> <term>Magha</term> <term>Uttara Phalguni</term> <term>Hasta</term> <term>Svati</term> <term>Anuradha</term> <term>Mula</term> <term>Uttara Ashadha</term> <term>Uttara Bhadrapada</term> <term>Revati</term>

**Now, the Lunar Days <term>Tithis</term>.**
The five days at the end of a lunar month should be abandoned. Excluding the "Empty" days <note>Rikta tithis: 4th, 9th, and 14th</note>, the eighth day, and the New Moon, the rest are acceptable. Some accept the eighth day of the dark fortnight for marriage.

**Now, the Days of the Week.**
The days of the auspicious planets <note>Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday</note> are praised. The days of the Sun and Saturn <note>Sunday and Saturday</note> are mediocre. The day of the son of the Earth <note>Tuesday/Mars</note> should always be abandoned. These are also considered "twilight" blemishes on the lunar days of the God of Love and the Sun.

**Now, the Ten Great Blemishes <term>Doshas</term> in Marriage.**
<term>1. Kick (Latta)</term> <term>2. Fall (Pata)</term> <term>3. Union (Yuti)</term> <term>4. Obstruction (Vedha)</term> <term>5. Seventh House (Jamitra)</term> <term>6. Fivefold Mercury (Budha-panchaka)</term> <term>7. Single Spike (Ekargala)</term> <term>8. Minor Planet (Upagraha)</term> <term>9. Declination Equality (Kranti-samya)</term> <term>10. Burnt Day (Dagdha-tithi)</term>

**Now, the Fall <term>Pata</term>.**
At the end of the astrological yogas named Harshana, Vaidhriti, Sadhya, Ganda, and Vyatipata, the lunar mansion that occurs is said to be "fallen" by the Pata blemish.

**Now, the Union <term>Yuti</term> (3).**

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

Even during a favorable lunar transit, journeys, entering a new home, and auspicious marriage ceremonies are not desired if certain astrological "kicks" <note>original: "latta," a technical term for a planet's malefic influence striking a specific star</note> are present. Just as with the movement of planets, one must avoid the influence of horses and cows <note>likely referring to specific animal-themed astrological divisions</note>. Whether the star is naturally auspicious or inauspicious, it must be avoided if afflicted. These planetary intersections and "falls" are considered particularly harmful in the regions of Surajya, Kacch, Shankha, and Malwa. Now, we shall discuss the defect known as Jamitra (The Seventh House Defect).

->The Jamitra Chart<-

The fourteenth star from the marriage star is called Jamitra. Furthermore, if a planet is situated in the seventh house <note>the house of partnership</note> from either the rising sign (Lagna) or the Moon, it is considered a Jamitra defect. This also occurs if the planet falls within specific degree segments (Bana-shagala). If Venus is in the 1st, 5th, 8th, or 11th house, it also relates to this calculation.

Some say these should be avoided based on specific days. If the remainder after dividing by nine is "with a thorn" <note>sashalya</note>, it yields extremely censurable results. Some authorities suggest adding the marriage date (Tithi) to the rising sign for this calculation. However, this specific teaching is primarily for those living in the present time.

## The Junction of Lunar Days:
<note>original: "Tithi-Ganda"</note>
The junction points <note>Ganda-anta; the 'end of the knot' or transition between certain lunar days</note> are said to grant death in activities such as journeys and marriages. However, the fault arising from the junction of lunar days and other factors is destroyed if the Moon <note>original: "Shitarashmih" (the cool-rayed one)</note> is situated in the eleventh house <note>the house of gains</note>. This is according to the Yodharika-Dharma.

## The Equality of Declination.
<note>original: "Kranti-Samya"</note>
The yoga of equal punishment <note>Sama-danda-yoga</note> occurs when the Sun and Moon have equal declination. The possibility of this equality is only achievable through great mathematical calculation. Currently, it occurs in the proximity of the Ganda and Shubha yogas. Even more subtle than that is the 'Pata' <note>an astronomical node or intersection</note>, which was produced with joy by Chandayudha.

The "Jaw of Death" <note>Yama-danshtra</note> occurs in the final asterisms starting from Mula; in the earlier ones, it is called "Dhora." This too is auspicious if the Moon is bright and situated in a position of gain.

The triad of junctions <note>Ganda-anta</note> grants death at birth; just as it gives evil results then, it should be considered similarly for journeys. However, if joined with auspicious planets in the house of gain, the fault becomes small.

# Muhurtasindhu

By a rapid method, having understood the <term>Bhabhoga</term><note>The total duration of a Nakshatra's span</note> from the <term>Panchanga</term><note>The five-limbed Hindu almanac</note> on any given day, one should multiply it by the specific ghatis <note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> and divide by the total sum; these then become the "clear" or corrected values. Following that, the four <term>Visha-ghatikas</term><note>Inauspicious "poisonous" moments within a Nakshatra</note> are calculated. The fixed constants mentioned for these poisonous moments, when multiplied by the elapsed and remaining portions of the Nakshatra and divided by sixty (60), become corrected. These four ghatis of time destroy the blemish of the "poisonous" period. If the Moon is in a gentle sign, or aspected by a friendly planet, or positioned in its own divisional chart, or if the Lord of the Ascendant is similarly placed, then the results associated with those combinations will surely manifest. Through the strength of the Moon or Jupiter, the following conditions like "Wind" and others come to be.

# ->The Ocean of Auspicious Moments<-
<note>original: "Muhurtasindhu"</note>

The results should be understood as follows. **Now, the results of the divisions:**
<note>term: Amshaphalam (results of the Navamsha or ninth-part divisions of a zodiac sign)</note>
A woman married when the rising division is Taurus becomes wealthy; if in the division of Pisces, she will be full of joy. This was indeed spoken by the sage Shaunaka. The divisions of Cancer, Libra, Gemini, and Virgo are considered auspicious. The division of Sagittarius is also auspicious. The "Best of the Class" <note>term: Vargottama (when a planet occupies the same sign in both the main chart and the ninth-part division)</note> is always auspicious. 

If the Lord of the Body <note>the planet ruling the rising sign</note> has set <note>is too close to the sun</note>, it causes the destruction of the couple. If the division is occupied by a cruel planet <note>a malefic like Mars or Saturn</note>, there will be loss; if the Moon is present in such a division, it portends death.

**Now, the Purification of the Ascendant:**
<note>term: Lagnashuddhi (ensuring the rising sign is free from astrological flaws)</note>
In marriage, the twelfth division <note>Dwadasamsha</note> causes the destruction of wealth. The eighth sign from the birth moon or the birth ascendant brings death. The fourth sign should be considered based on its merits, but the twelfth is highly problematic. One must avoid the eighth house and the eighth division. If the lords of the eighth house from the birth star or birth ascendant are placed in the wedding ascendant, those signs and divisions must be abandoned. 

However, if Scorpio or Taurus are the eighth signs, this fault does not apply. Furthermore, if there is friendship between the Lord of Birth and the Lord of the Eighth, the eighth house does not cause harm. Alternatively, if the Lord of the Ascendant or the Lord of the Eighth is in a center <note>houses 1, 4, 7, or 10</note> and is aspected by a benefic, the fault is nullified.

According to the opinion of Trivikrama:
The Sun, Moon, and Mars should be avoided in the 1st house. The Moon, Saturn, and the Ascendant Lord should be avoided in the 6th house. All planets are forbidden in the 7th house, though Jupiter and the Moon in the 7th are considered neutral. Mercury, Mars, Jupiter, Venus, and the Ascendant Lord are forbidden in the 8th house. According to the opinion of all teachers: Saturn in the 12th, any planet in its own 3rd house, and Venus—like the Moon—are not praised. 

**Now, the Calculation of the Twenty-Point Strength:**
<note>term: Vishopaka (a system of points used to evaluate planetary strength)</note>
Two points each for Mercury and Venus; five for the Moon; three for Jupiter; and 1.5 points each for Saturn, Mars, and the Sun. <note>The text continues to detail specific point deductions and additions based on planetary placements in various houses like the 11th, 8th, and 6th.</note>

**Now, the Scissor Formation:**
<note>term: Kartari (an astrological configuration where a house or planet is "snipped" between two malefic planets)</note>
When two malefic planets are placed in the 12th and 2nd houses from either the Ascendant or the Moon, it is called a "Scissor Formation." This brings death, poverty, and sorrow.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments
## Page 120

If the planets are situated in the eighth and second houses from the rising sign <note>Lagna</note>, it is known as a Great Scissor <term>Maha-Kartari: a configuration where the house is 'cut' or squeezed between two malefic planets</term>. Now, the exceptions to this Scissor configuration: If the faster-moving planet is in retrograde motion, the Scissor effect does not occur; so says the Great Ancestor <note>Pitamaha, likely referring to the sage Brahma or an early astronomical authority</note>. Furthermore, if the two malefic planets forming the Scissor are in their enemy's sign, their sign of debilitation, or are combust <note>too close to the sun to be visible</note>, they do not cause the Scissor defect.

If benefic planets are placed in the trines <note>1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note> or the centers <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note>, or if they are in the third or eleventh houses, the sage Badarayana says the Scissor defect is destroyed. Indeed, the defect born of the Scissor does not occur if it involves two benefic planets. When the rising sign is joined by a benefic planet, the malefic Scissor is non-existent. Just as the darkness of dawn vanishes at the rising of the sun, all defects—including the single-bolt <term>Ekargala</term>, planetary falls, kicks <term>Latta</term>, the seventh-house Scissor, and rising/setting defects—are destroyed when the rising sign is endowed with the strength of the Moon and the Sun.

### The Twilight Hour (Godhuli)

The fourth house from the Sun <note>Abhijit Muhurta</note> and the seventh house from the rising sign are both known as the "Dust of the Cows" <term>Godhuli: the time of sunset when returning cattle kick up dust</term>. In marriage, both of these provide sons and grandsons. Among the people of the East and Kalinga, the Twilight Hour is considered primary. However, the Abhijit moment <note>midday</note> is considered the primary destroyer of defects in all regions. When the Sun is at the meridian, the moment called Abhijit destroys all defects, just as Shiva destroyed the three cities of the demons.

In this Abhijit moment, one must only avoid Mars or the Moon in the eighth house. In the Twilight Hour, one must carefully examine the strength of the Moon. If the Moon is in the 2nd, 3rd, or 11th houses, the Twilight Hour is considered twice as auspicious. If a perfectly pure rising sign <note>Lagna</note> cannot be found, then the Twilight Hour is advised; however, if a pure rising sign is available, the Twilight Hour is not as beneficial. One should not perform a wedding in the Twilight Hour if the specific bad timings <term>Kulika</term>, the declination parity <term>Kranti-samya</term>, or if the Moon is in the 8th or 6th house from the rising sign.

The sage Bhrigu says: The dust raised by the hooves of cows being driven by the sticks of cowherds at the end of the day brings various riches, children, health, and good fortune to beautiful women in marriage. At that time, one need not consider the lunar mansion <term>Nakshatra</term>, the lunar day <term>Tithi</term>, the half-day <term>Karana</term>, the rising sign, or the yoga. The dust of the cows raised at sunset removes all sins of men. From the time the Sun looks like saffron until the stars appear, as long as the cow-dust is in the sky, so long...

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

...is considered an auspicious ascendant <note>Sanskrit: *Lagnam*; the specific zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</note> by the wise. When the sun appears like a dense mass <note>referring to the visual distortion of the sun near the horizon</note> in the winter season, it is half-set; in the month of Magha <note>late January to February</note>, it is fully set. This "Godhuli" <note>literally "cow-dust" time; the period at sunset when returning cattle kick up dust, considered naturally auspicious</note> is complete at sunset. During the rainy season, this time should be applied in three ways for all auspicious works. From the end of the day until the third part of the sun's disk is visible in the west, and for two Ghatikas <note>approximately 48 minutes</note> thereafter, the sages say, is the Godhuli period. In the east, when the colors have mostly faded, they call it the twilight time, which is not desired for auspicious acts. As long as the dust from the cows' hooves does not settle, that period is an auspicious ascendant for the purification of the mind in marriage. The wise should not perform the marriage rite at the beginning of the night on a Saturday, nor on a Thursday after the sun has set. Godhuli is primarily prescribed for the Warrior class <note>Kshatriyas</note> and others; if the Lord of the Ascendant or Jupiter casts a glance <note>Drishti; an astrological aspect</note> upon it, there is no defect. These [restrictions] are to be avoided in the Gauda <note>ancient Bengal/North-East India</note> and other regions.

### The Installation of the Family Deity

Under the lunar mansions <note>Nakshatras</note> of Mrigashira, Revati, Chitra, Anuradha, Swati, the three Uttaras <note>Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada</note>, Rohini, Hasta, Ashwini, and Pushya—on auspicious weekdays, excluding the Bhadra <note>an inauspicious lunar day/Karana</note>—the installation should be done in a fixed ascendant.

### General Marriage Rituals

All marriage rituals should be examined according to the marriage lunar mansions; one need not look at the strength of the Moon <note>Himadyuti</note> here. On the ninth, third, or sixth day prior to the marriage, the coloring, the ritual circle, the oil, and the auspicious rites [begin]. Here, first is the anointing of the bride with oil, and afterwards the oiling of the groom. This occurs in the first watch of the night. Some say the bride should be sprinkled with the oil left over from the groom. Then follows the binding of the bracelet <note>Kankanabandhanam</note>; this is done to the bride first. The untying of the bracelet is done to the groom first.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments
<note>original: "Muhurta Sindhu"</note>

The precise <term>Ascendant</term><note>Lagna: the point of the zodiac rising on the eastern horizon</note> is determined by the vertical and horizontal alignment of the Sun's sign and degree within the table. Add the desired <term>ghatikas</term><note>A unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> to the value found in the corresponding cell. Where the horizontal and vertical coordinates meet, that value—combined with the desired time and adjusted by subtracting the clear time—should be multiplied by sixty and divided by the difference in minutes to reach the exact calculation.

### On the Calculation of the Tenth House
<note>The Tenth House or "Midheaven" relates to one's profession and public life.</note>

Now, the calculation for the <term>Hour Angle</term><note>Nata: the time elapsed since the planet was at the meridian</note> used for the Tenth House: The "Eastern Hour Angle" is found by subtracting the desired time from the half-duration of the day or night. Conversely, if the half-duration of the day or night is subtracted from the desired time, it becomes the "Western Hour Angle." 

In simpler terms: half the day or night minus the elapsed time of day or night equals the Eastern Hour Angle. The elapsed time of day or night minus the half-duration equals the Western Hour Angle. Just as with the Ascendant, by adding these hours to the coordinates of the Sun’s sign and degrees, the Tenth House is determined. Note that in certain calculations, this may result in the Fourth House <insert>the opposite point</insert>.

### On the Calculation of the Other Houses
<note>Bhava: the twelve divisions of the celestial sphere</note>

To find the remaining houses: take the difference between the Ascendant and the Tenth House and divide it by six. Add this sixth part to the Ascendant to find the <term>junction</term><note>Sandhi: the cusp or boundary between two astrological houses</note> of the first house. Adding it again gives the Second House, then the junction of the Second House, then the Third House, and then the junction of the Third House. 

Furthermore, by adding this same sixth part to the Fourth House, one finds the junction of the Fourth House, followed by the Fifth House, the junction of the Fifth House, the Sixth House, and finally the junction of the Sixth House. By continuing to add these increments to each house and junction in sequence, all twelve houses will be successfully established.

<summary>This page provides mathematical formulas for calculating the Tenth House (Midheaven) and the boundaries of the twelve astrological houses using the Ascendant and time-based hour angles.</summary>
<keywords>astrology, Ascendant, Tenth House, Bhava, Sandhi, time calculation, Muhurta Sindhu, mathematical astronomy</keywords>

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

Following this method, after determining the houses <note>original: "bhavan," referring to the twelve astrological houses</note>, if the Ascendant is pure and possesses its divisional strengths <note>original: "savargam," referring to the Shadvarga or six-fold division of a sign</note>, it is considered a most excellent Ascendant. When planets are positioned in the middle of a house, they yield full results; if they are at the junctions <note>original: "sandhi," the border between two houses</note>, they yield no result. 

**Vyasa** states: A combination of six or five divisional strengths brings auspiciousness; four divisions are acceptable, but three divisions will cause loss. 

**Vashistha** says: If the Ascendant is occupied by four planets that are favorable and possess strength, it is considered auspicious even if the six-fold divisions are unfavorable. This is the opinion of **Gautama**, **Galava**, and others.

### The Twenty-One Major Blemishes
Although previously mentioned, these twenty-one impediments <note>term: "doshas" — astrological flaws that render a time inauspicious</note> are stated here for the sake of memory:

1. Flaws arising from a bad Five-Fold Calendar <note>term: "Panchang" — the five limbs of time: date, day, constellation, yoga, and karana</note>
2. Solar Transit <note>original: "Sankranti"</note>
3. The Moon joined with a planet
4. The Scissor-grip <note>term: "Kartari" — when the Ascendant or Moon is hemmed in by malefic planets</note>
5. The Moon in the 6th or 8th house from the Ascendant
6. The three types of "End-Points" <note>term: "Gandanta" — inauspicious junctions between signs or constellations</note>
7. Weakness in the six-fold divisions
8. Venus in an enemy's sign
9. Mars in an unfavorable position
10. Flaws in the 1st or 7th houses
11. An inauspicious hour <note>original: "Kumuhoortah"</note>
12. The Ascendant being the 8th house from the birth sign of the groom or bride
13. Poisonous time-intervals <note>original: "Visha Nadya"</note>
14. Unspecified portions of constellations
15. The "Single-Bolt" obstruction <note>original: "Ekargala"</note>
16. Flaws of the weekday
17. Constellations marked by portents
18. The constellation in which an eclipse occurred
19. Piercing by a malefic planet
20. Approach of a malefic planet
21. The "Fall" <note>term: "Pata" — specifically the astronomical nodes or specific latitudinal alignments</note>

Others to be avoided include: unseasonal rain (1), fall of hailstones (2), excessive thunder (3), snowfall (4), violent winds (5), halos around the sun or moon (6), mock suns or moons (7), rainbows (8), and bad combinations arising from the date, constellation, or day (9). These aforementioned should be avoided whenever possible.

### Consideration of Adverse Events
If a death occurs within three generations <note>original: "tripaurushe"</note> after the marriage has been fixed, the wedding should take place after one month. However, if a Guru <note>note: can refer to a spiritual teacher or a paternal elder</note> dies, the wedding should occur after one year. A marriage is considered "fixed" once the formal promise <note>original: "Vag-dana"</note> is made or the ancestral invocation <note>term: "Nandi Shraddha" — a ritual performed at the start of auspicious ceremonies</note> has been performed. This should be understood according to local custom. After the period of ritual impurity <note>original: "sutaka"</note> has passed, the ceremony may be performed following a purification rite. This concludes the section on marriage.

### The Entry of the Bride
The "Bride's Entry" <note>original: "Vadhupraveshah"</note> refers to the first time a newly married woman enters her husband's home. This should occur on the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 14th, 5th, 7th, or 9th day from the wedding...

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments
<note>Original title: Muhurta-Sindhu</note>

During auspicious days, after the fifth year, one may act according to desire regarding odd months and years. <term>Narada</term><note>A legendary sage and authority on astrology and law</note> states: If a woman enters her husband's house in an even month or an even year <insert>after the marriage</insert>, she takes away the life of her husband and meets with misfortune herself. When the results of the marriage are coming to fruition, a wise man should not perform the bride's entry, the binding or releasing of a vow, or a second marriage within the second year; so say the sages <term>Vasistha</term>, <term>Atri</term>, and <term>Parashara</term>.

The entry is auspicious under the following <term>Nakshatras</term><note>Lunar mansions or star constellations</note>: Uttara-Phalguni, Uttara-Ashadha, Uttara-Bhadrapada, Rohini, Hasta, Ashwini, Pushya, Shravana, Abhijit, Mrigashirsha, Revati, Chitra, Anuradha, Shravana, Dhanishta, Mula, Magha, and Swati. These are favorable on the days of the Sun, Mars, and Mercury <note>Sunday, Tuesday, and Wednesday</note>, provided it is a fixed or dual-natured <term>Lagna</term><note>Ascendant sign</note> and falls on the <term>Purna</term>, <term>Jaya</term>, or <term>Nanda</term> lunar days during the marriage month. 

Some authorities accept Wednesday as a favorable day. They forbid constellations other than those specified for marriage and state that the bride's entry should only occur at night. In the constellations favorable for marriage, a night entry during an auspicious moment with a fixed sign rising is praised. Here, the "Two Evils of Venus" <note>referring to the combustion or retrograde motion of Venus</note> are not considered a prohibition.

->The Bride's Entry<-

Now, the auspicious timing for returning from the husband's house to the father's house: This should be done when the constellations are not of the "dreadful" or "fierce" categories, on days other than Saturday, Sunday, or Tuesday, during a favorable lunar day and Ascendant, and in the absence of "bad yogas" <note>inuspicious planetary combinations</note>.

Now, regarding the lighting of lamps during the <term>Deepavali</term><note>Festival of Lights</note> festival: When the strength of the Moon and the stars is favorable, in the evening during the Aries Ascendant, the lustration ceremony <note>ritual waving of lamps</note> is performed by women. For this reason, even a married man attains the full status of a householder through this lamp-lighting ceremony on that day. Therefore, on the day of the Festival of Lights, both the first entry of the bride and the second return <note>Dviragamana</note> should be performed only when the Moon and stars are pure.

Regarding the period immediately following the Festival of Lights <note>Deepavali</note>, one must consider the setting of Jupiter and Venus, as well as the transition of the Sun into Leo.

### On the Second Entry into the Husband's House
The "Second Entry" <term>Dvirāgama: the ritual return of a bride to her husband's home after the initial wedding</term> refers to the second time a married woman goes to her husband. This should occur in an odd-numbered year and month from the time of the wedding. It is auspicious when the Sun is in Aries, Scorpio, or Aquarius, during the bright fortnight <note>Shukla-paksha</note>, and on a favorable day of the week. The Sun and Jupiter must be astrologically purified <term>Shuddhi: a state of planetary strength and purity</term> for the groom. The favorable lunar mansions <term>Nakshatras</term> are: Hasta, Ashwini, Pushya, Abhijit, the three Uttaras, Rohini, Swati, Punarvasu, Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha, Mrigashirsha, Revati, Chitra, Anuradha, and Mula. Using the 2nd, 3rd, 6th, or 12th signs as the ascendant <term>Lagna</term>, one must avoid having Venus directly in front or to the right. A child, a pregnant woman, a new bride, or a traveler should not journey when Venus is in front or to the right. If they do, the child may die, the pregnant woman may suffer a miscarriage, the new bride may become barren, and the traveler's purpose will be ruined.

### Exceptions to these Restrictions
In times of national calamity, royal oppression, or famine; or during a wedding procession, a pilgrimage, or out of fear of the king; or during the initial entry of the bride, the "Venus defect" <term>Shukra-dosha</term> does not apply. Similarly, if the journey is within the same village, or if it is to the father's house, or if the bride has reached puberty <note>literally "the appearance of breasts and menses"</note>, the Venus defect is ignored. In the case of reaching puberty, the purification of the Sun and Jupiter is considered optional. However, if she is at her father's house when she reaches puberty, the purification of the Sun and Jupiter is required. If the bride goes to her husband's home during an auspicious ascendant, with a strong Moon and a favorable lunar day <term>Tithi</term>, even if Venus is in front or to the right, the fault is considered minor due to the necessity of the duty. Furthermore, there is no fault for those belonging to the lineages <term>Gotras</term> of Bhrigu, Angiras, Vatsa, Vashistha, Kashyapa, and Atri. When the Moon is in the mansions from Revati to Krittika, Venus is considered "downward-facing" and causes no fault.

### On the New Bride's First Cooking
The new bride should perform her first cooking ritual <term>Pākakarma</term> under the lunar mansions of Mrigashirsha, the three Uttaras, Pushya, Krittika, Hasta, the three Shravanas <note>Shravana, Dhanishta, Shatabhisha</note>, Rohini, Vishakha, or Revati. This should be done on an auspicious lunar day, excluding Tuesday and Sunday. The cooking should be initiated during a "fixed" ascendant <term>Sthira Lagna</term>, when the 4th house is pure, the 7th house is strong, and the 8th house is free of planets.

## 9. The Establishment of the Sacred Fire

The establishment of the sacred fire <note>Sanskrit: Agnyadhana; the ritual of formally setting up the three sacrificial fires</note> should be performed at the time of marriage or at the time of the division of inheritance. It should take place during the northern transit of the sun <note>Uttarayana; the period between the winter and summer solstices</note> and when the planetary lord of one's own Vedic branch is rising. In some cases, it may also be done during the southern transit <note>Dakshinayana</note>, or during a sacrifice performed by one's father, or using the domestic fire <note>Upasana-agni</note>. It should be done when Jupiter and Venus are visible <note>not combust or hidden by the sun's glare</note> and in the absence of a decayed or intercalary month <note>Kshaya or Adhika Masa; lunar months added or removed to align the calendar</note>. It requires the permission of the father and elder brother, and the strength of the Moon. 

The ceremony should avoid the "Empty" lunar days <note>Rikta tithis: the 4th, 9th, and 14th days of the lunar fortnight</note> and should not be performed on a Saturday. The following lunar mansions <note>Nakshatras</note> are recommended: Jyeshtha, Krittika, Tishya (Pushya), Mrigashirsha, Revati, the three Uttaras (Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada), Rohini, and Vishakha. Some also suggest Hasta, Chitra, and Pushya. 

The 11th, 4th, 12th, and 10th signs are favorable for the rising sign <note>Lagna</note> or its ninth division <note>Navamsha</note>. The Moon should not be in the first house. If the ritual is on a Sunday, the Sun should be in the 9th house; on Monday, the Moon in the 5th; on Tuesday, Mars in the 3rd; on Thursday, Jupiter in the 11th; on Wednesday, Mercury in the 2nd, 11th, 10th, 5th, or 3rd. In these positions, the fire remains perpetual and brings auspicious results. 

If the rising sign is Sagittarius with Jupiter present, or if Mars is in Aries in the 7th or 10th house, or if the Sun, Moon, Saturn, or Rahu are in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses, it is an auspicious combination. If the Moon is in the 8th house, the wife perishes; if a malefic planet is in the 8th, the performer himself perishes; if a benefic is in the 8th, both suffer disease. If the lord of the rising sign is in its sign of debilitation or defeated in planetary war, the performer meets an evil end. One should not establish the fire when Jupiter, the Moon, or Mars are debilitated, combust, defeated, in an enemy's house, or in the 8th house. Furthermore, the ritual should not begin in the month of Chaitra even if the Sun is in Aries, nor in the fourth quarter of the day, nor during the southern transit at night.

---

### On the Timing and Names of the Cooked Sacrifices

The Cooked Sacrifices <note>Paka-yajnas; simpler domestic offerings</note> are performed at their respective specified times. There are seven types: 1. Establishment of the Fire, 2. The Daily Fire Offering <note>Agnihotra</note>, 3. New and Full Moon Sacrifices, 4. The Four-Monthly Sacrifices <note>Chaturmasya, consisting of the Vaishvadeva, Varunapraghasa, Sakamedha, and Shunasiriya festivals</note>, 5. Animal Sacrifice <note>Pashubandha</note>, 6. The Sautramani Sacrifice, and 7. The Cooked Sacrifice <note>Paka-yajna</note>. These are the seven forms of Havis-sacrifices <note>offerings of grain or ghee</note>.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

The Shodashi (4), Atiratra (5), Vajapeya (6), and Aptoryama (7) <note>These are specific types of complex Vedic sacrifices involving the pressing of the Soma plant</note>—these are the seven forms of the **Soma-sacrifice**. Now, the seven forms of the **Cooked-offering sacrifices** <term>Paka-yajna: simple domestic sacrifices involving cooked food rather than complex Soma rituals</term>: The Shravana rite (1), the Ashvayuji rite (2), the Agrahayani rite (3), the Ashtaka of cakes (4), the Ashtaka of meat (5), the Ashtaka of vegetables (6), and the Ashtaka of the rainy season (7). It is said that these Cooked-offering sacrifices should be performed by setting aside defects such as the setting of Venus or Jupiter, eclipses, intercalary months <note>an extra month added to the lunar calendar to keep it in sync with the solar year</note>, and the transition of the sun into a new sign. For the Soma-sacrifices, they should be performed in the summer or winter seasons when the Sun is in the 2nd, 7th, 9th, or 12th zodiac signs, on the lunar days, weekdays, and lunar mansions prescribed for the establishment of the sacred fires.

## Regarding the Great Fire-Offering

During the northern course of the sun <note>Uttarayana: the period between the winter and summer solstices, considered spiritually auspicious</note>, on a day free from the aforementioned defects, on a favorable lunar day and under an auspicious rising sign, specifically on the lunar days of the waxing moon, and on the weekdays of the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus, or Jupiter. In the lunar mansions of Ardra, Shravana, Rohini, Purva Bhadrapada, or Hasta—as well as those mansions prescribed for the establishment of the sacred fires—the sages have declared that the **Great Rudra Fire-Offerings** and others should be performed.

## Regarding the Final Offering

The **Final Offering** <term>Purnahuti: the "full offering" that completes a ritual</term> should be made on a "Full" lunar day <note>the 5th, 10th, or 15th days of the lunar fortnight</note>, in the lunar mansions previously mentioned for offerings, on an auspicious weekday, and under an auspicious rising sign.

## Regarding the Ritual Bath

The **Ablution Bath** <term>Avabhrutha-snana: the ceremonial bath taken at the conclusion of a sacrifice to purify the performer</term> should take place on the "Nanda," "Jaya," or "Purna" lunar days, under an auspicious rising sign, on a favorable weekday, and during an auspicious astrological alignment. In these cases, one should understand the cancellation of malefic influences in sequence: On the **Base**, one becomes dependent on others; on the **Seat**, one is endowed with morality; for the King's chief officials, it brings peace to the subjects; on the **Tablet**, the result is as before; on the **Lion-seat**, one becomes like a lion, fond of battle and unconquerable even by ministers; on the **Throne**, one becomes radiant and of fearsome form, yet fickle-minded, prone to great anger, and a source of suffering for the subjects.

In this regard, even the piercing <note>astrological interference or "vedha"</note> by malefic planets is considered censurable. When the Moon is in an auspicious state and the birth-consecration occurs in a masculine zodiac sign, the King or the Brahmin becomes a sharer in the grace of Shiva. Now, the necessary considerations for these are: for a Brahmin performing the *Vajapeya* <note>a high-ranking Vedic sacrifice</note> and others; for the master of horses, the purity of the horse; for the master of elephants, the elephant; and for the King, the purity of the chariot must be understood. # The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

On a Friday, Wednesday, or Thursday, under a constellation <note>Nakshatra</note> that is not "fierce" or "dreadful," during a favorable ascendant <note>Lagna</note>, and free from bad astrological combinations <note>Kuyoga</note> or the *Vishti* period <note>an inauspicious timing in the lunar calendar</note>; excluding the dark fortnight of the month of Ashadha and the months of Bhadrapada and Ashvina; up until the tenth day of the dark fortnight; and while Jupiter and Venus are visible in the sky—one should perform the Ritual Bath with Flowers and the Single-Garment Bath. ### Now, the Consecration of a King <insert>10</insert>

When the Sun is in its northern course <note>Uttarayana</note>, or when the Sun is in Scorpio, Libra, or Virgo; for universal emperors or regional lords, excluding the months of Ashadha, Shravana, and Bhadrapada; also excluding intercalary months <note>Malamasa</note> or decayed months <note>Kshayamasa</note>; while Jupiter and Venus are visible and the Moon is strong; when Mars, the Sun, the lord of the birth sign, and the lord of the tenth house are visible; and when the birth period is strong. 

A local governor <note>Durgadhipa</note> should be consecrated like a regional lord. For a village headman, the ceremony should avoid the *Rikta* lunar days <note>the 4th, 9th, and 14th days, considered "empty"</note> and bad combinations like *Bhadra*. It should occur on a Thursday, Monday, Sunday, Wednesday, or Friday when those planets are strong and visible. Even a Tuesday is acceptable for the consecration of a warrior-caste <note>Kshatriya</note> king. Some authorities forbid the month of Chaitra.

The favorable constellations are the three "Later" ones <note>Uttara Phalguni, Uttara Ashadha, Uttara Bhadrapada</note>, Rohini, Mrigashira, Jyeshtha, Hasta, Ashvini, Pushya, Abhijit, Shravana, Anuradha, Revati, and Chitra. The ascendant should be a "Head-rising" sign <note>Shirshodaya - signs that rise head-first, considered auspicious</note> such as the 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 3rd, 11th, or 12th. Relative to the birth ascendant or birth sign, it should be in an "Increasing" house <note>Upachaya: the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th</note>. 

**The Placement of Planets:**
*   **Malefic planets** <note>Sun, Mars, Saturn, Rahu, Ketu</note> should be in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th houses.
*   **Benefic planets** <note>Moon, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus</note> should be in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 10th, 9th, 5th, or 2nd houses.
*   In a Head-rising division: Jupiter in the ascendant or a trine <note>1st, 5th, or 9th</note>; Mars in the 6th; Venus in the 10th.

A king consecrated under these combinations enjoys the Goddess of Royal Fortune. However:
*   If malefic planets are in the 2nd or 12th: he becomes destitute.
*   If in the 1st (ascendant): he becomes sickly.
*   If in the 7th or 4th: he is deposed from his position.
*   If in the 5th: he is deprived of all happiness.
*   If in the 10th: his festivals and duties are ruined.
*   If in the 8th: he will have a short life.
*   If the Moon is in the 12th, 8th, or 6th: it destroys his life-force.
*   If malefic planets are in the 3rd, 6th, or 11th, and Jupiter is in the 10th and Mercury in the 4th: the Goddess of Royal Fortune is secured.

**Now, the Construction of the Assembly Hall:**
On auspicious days, lunar dates, and under favorable constellations, when the transit of planets is pure, one should construct the hall in the shape of a bow, with the royal throne placed in the center.

**Now, the Entry into the Assembly Hall:**
Having placed the great elephant with its banner in front, followed by horses with their riders, chariots, doorkeepers, and ministers, the King should enter at the time designated by the royal priest, during an auspicious planetary alignment for kings. After performing the worship of Ganesha and other deities, he should ascend the throne of fortune. He should then satisfy the craftsmen and the priest with gifts of cows, land, and gold.

**Now, the Auspicious Time for Binding the Royal Band:**
This should be done on the days prescribed for the Royal Consecration <note>Abhisheka</note> within houses, cities, or villages.

**Now, the Auspicious Time for the Pavilion Tent:**

On the days of Venus, Jupiter, the Moon, or the Sun; under "Upward-facing" constellations; in a stable zodiac sign joined by benefics; with auspicious planets in the cardinal houses; on dates other than the "Empty" ones; and in the absence of any "Evil Unions" <note>Kuyoga: specific inauspicious planetary combinations</note>.

**Now, the Consecration of the Crown Prince:**
This is to be performed in the same manner as the Royal Consecration.

**Now, the Auspicious Time for the King to Take Up the Whisk, Umbrella, Palanquin, and Throne:**
Under Rohini, the three "Later" stars, Anuradha, Chitra, Mrigashira, Revati, Abhijit, Ashwini, Hasta, Jyeshtha, and Shravana; on the "Victory" or "Joy" lunar dates; on auspicious days and under auspicious signs; with the tenth and eighth houses being pure. ### The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

### Muhurta-Sindhu

Whether facing Mercury or facing Mars, even a King equal to Indra <note>The king of the gods</note> will return with his army destroyed. This is a common fault for all men. Regarding the fault of facing Venus <note>Prati-shukra: traveling in the direction where Venus is currently located</note>, some say it does not apply to kings on a victory march <term>Vijayayatra: a formal military expedition for conquest</term>. However, that claim is hollow. "Victory march" here specifically refers to a journey started on the festival of *Vijayadashami* <note>The tenth day of the lunar month of Ashvin, traditionally auspicious for kings to begin campaigns</note>. For journeys started then, the fault of facing Venus and others does indeed exist. For the previously mentioned lineages <term>Gotras</term>, and when the Moon is in the constellations from Revati to Mrigashira, there is no fault. The auspicious timing for a journey is only for those whose birth details are known. For those with unknown birth details, timing should be determined through divination <term>Prashna</term> or omens.

**Garga** <note>An ancient sage and authority on astronomy/astrology</note> says: A journey is auspicious during a favorable planetary period <term>Dasha</term>. If the Eight-fold Division <term>Ashtakavarga</term> is auspicious, the journey is balanced; if the current Ascendant <term>Lagna</term> or lunar day <term>Tithi</term> is weak, it is considered inferior. If the birth sign or birth ascendant is in the rising sign, or if their lords are there, or if the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses from the rising sign are occupied by the Sun, victory is certain for the lord of the earth <note>The King</note>. If the enemy's birth sign or ascendant, or their lords, are in the 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses from the traveler's sign, or if there are auspicious planetary divisions in the 4th or 7th houses, then victory is achieved. Traveling on the 1st, 3rd, 5th, or 7th birth-stars <term>Tara</term> is not desired.

#### Types of Journeys
1. **Short:** Up to 12 Yojanas <note>A Yojana is roughly 8-9 miles</note>.
2. **Medium:** Up to 25 Yojanas.
3. **Long:** Anything beyond that.

Additionally:
1. **War Expedition** <term>Yuddha-yatra</term>
2. **Pilgrimage** <term>Tirtha-yatra</term>
3. **Business/Profit Journey** <term>Labha-yatra</term>

#### Timing for Journeys
In all journeys, one should not travel when Venus is set <note>Invisible/combust</note>. Likewise, one should not travel when the Lord of the Birth Sign or the Lord of the Birth Period is set. For pilgrimages, the setting of Jupiter and Venus must be avoided. Jupiter in Leo or in its sign of debilitation should also be avoided. A person desiring a pilgrimage should not go when the "Serpent Weapon" <note>A specific astrological configuration</note> is active, or when the planets are in "infant," "old," or "debilitated" states, except for the Gautami <note>Godavari River</note> or Gaya when Jupiter is in Aquarius. On the fourth or fifth lunar days...

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments
<note>original: "Muhurtasindhu"</note>

**Narada** <note>A legendary sage and celestial messenger in Hindu tradition</note> states: Travel on the sixth, eighth, and twelfth lunar days, as well as on the "Empty" days <note>Rikta: the 4th, 9th, and 14th lunar days, considered hollow or unlucky for new ventures</note>, the New Moon, and the Full Moon, or on the first day of the bright fortnight, leads to death or loss of wealth. **Now, regarding specific months:** When the Moon and Sun are in the same Solstice <note>Samayanatve: both in the northern or both in the southern course</note>, travel in all directions is auspicious, whether by day or by night.

---

->**Results of the Weekdays**<-

| Sun | Moon | Mars | Merc | Jup | Ven | Sat | Weekdays |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| Loss | Strength/Defect | Disease | Happiness | Dearness | Enjoyment | Void | Results |

<note>This table correlates the day of the week with the predicted outcome of a journey started on that day.</note>

->**The Collection of Directional Spears**<-
<note>Dikshula: "Directional Spears" are specific directions to be avoided on certain days or times.</note>

| NE | | East | | SE |
|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| | Merc, Sat | Morning <br> <note>Nakshatras: Shravana, Jyeshtha</note> | Moon, Jup | |
| **North** | Midnight <br> <note>Mars, Merc, Uttara Bhadrapada</note> | | Midday <br> <note>Jup, Purva Bhadrapada</note> | **South** |
| | Merc, Sun | Evening <br> <note>Sun, Ven, Rohini</note> | Jup, Ven | |
| **NW** | | **West** | | **SW** |

---

In this system, the North is included within the East, and the South is included within the West. When the Solstices are different, one should avoid the intermediate directions at night and the Moon's direction <note>the Northwest</note>. During the four months of the rainy season <term>Chaturmasya: a period of traditional ascetic retreat</term> and during the bright fortnight of the month of Phalguna <note>February/March</note>, a "Great Journey" <note>Brihad-yatra: a long-distance or significant expedition</term> is forbidden. Likewise, when the Sun, Mars, or Saturn are in odd signs, or during a Solstice corrupted by an eclipse, neither a sea voyage nor a Great Journey should be undertaken. Similarly, a Great Journey is not advised when the Sun is in a dual-natured sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, or Pisces</note>. When the Sun is in the 2nd, 5th, or 8th house, a boat journey is forbidden. A Great or Medium journey is forbidden in the month of Bhadrapada <note>August/September</note>, and a pilgrimage <term>Tirthayatra: travel to a holy site</term> is forbidden in the month of Ashvina <note>September/October</note>.

### Consideration of the Yogini
<note>The Yoginis are eight female deities who rotate through the cardinal and intermediate directions. Their position determines whether a journey will be successful or fatal.</note>

Regarding the lunar days <term>Tithis: lunar days in the Hindu calendar</term>, it is taught that having the Yogini in front or to the left is generally not recommended. However, if the Yogini is joined with Rahu <note>The North Node of the Moon, considered a demonic shadow planet</note> and is positioned to the right or behind the traveler, she can destroy even a hundred thousand enemies. For the successful completion of a task, a Yogini facing the traveler is auspicious, but in the context of travel for war, a Yogini in front brings death. She is inauspicious on the right side, but brings auspicious light when on the left or behind.

Here, the contradiction regarding the effects of a single Yogini depending on the specific task is resolved by citing various authorities. According to the *Samarasara* <note>A text on military astrology</note>, which is rooted in the *Yamala* and *Narapatimula* traditions: for those seeking the Goddess of Victory or embarking on a war expedition, the Yogini is inauspicious on the left and auspicious on the right. Conversely, for a journey intended for financial gain <note>trade or profit</note>, she is auspicious on the left and inauspicious on the right, much like the interpretation of omens <term>Shakuna: the science of omens</term>.

Therefore, it is also stated in the *Jyotirnibandha*:
> For those seeking victory over an enemy, the Yogini is auspicious on the right. For those traveling for business affairs, she is declared best on the left.

If she stands with a sharp-edged sword in hand, she is auspicious on the right during war. However, this creates a distinction between two types of travel. It would then follow that the positions of the Moon and other planets should also differ for war expeditions, yet such a distinction is not commonly found in the texts.

Thus, another resolution is offered: In the *Yamala* tradition, if the Yogini is joined with Rahu, she is inauspicious when on the right. If she is not joined with Rahu, she is harmless due to her lack of strength. As it is said:
> If the Yogini is joined with Rahu, she grants auspiciousness on the right. If separated from Rahu, she is auspicious even on the left.

However, in my opinion, this remains an open choice <note>Vikalpa: a formal Vedic term for an optional rule</note>, as the division of subjects <note>between war and business</note> lacks a firm root and is based on interpretation.

If other faults are present and unavoidable, then the division of day and night for travel is considered. When the lunar mansion <note>Nakshatra</note> and the lunar day <note>Tithi</note> are endowed with good qualities, travel is forbidden <note>original: "niṣedhiṣma", likely a scribal variation for 'not forbidden' or 'specifically regulated'</note>. The sages praise traveling during the day when the lunar mansion is auspicious, and at night when the lunar day is auspicious. If both lack good qualities, one should bathe and then depart on Monday <note>Moon's day</note>; depart without bathing on Wednesday or Friday; depart without eating on Thursday or Sunday; and depart after eating on Tuesday or Saturday.

Now, the results of the Moon's position:
If the Moon is in front, it brings gain of wealth.
If to the right, it brings happiness and prosperity.
If behind, it brings death.
If to the left, it brings loss of wealth.
However, if the Moon is full and positioned in front, all faults are destroyed.

The sages provide various authorities for determining success: Garga emphasizes the dawn; Brihaspati <note>The preceptor of the gods, associated with the planet Jupiter</note> looks to the omens of birds; Angira focuses on mental enthusiasm; and Janardana <note>A name for Lord Vishnu</note> values the words of a learned priest. The dawn is auspicious except when facing East; the "cow-dust" hour <note>Godhuli: the period of sunset when returning cattle kick up dust</note> is auspicious except when facing West; the midnight hour is auspicious except when facing North; and the Abhijit period <note>A short interval around midday</note> is auspicious except when facing South.

Now, regarding travel: in all matters of movement, the specific durations <note>Ghatika: a unit of time equal to 24 minutes</note> of the Moon, the Yogini <note>A directional energy goddess</note>, and Rahu <note>The north node of the moon</note> must be clearly understood.

### The Ascendant for Travel
Travel during a "Head-rising" sign <note>Shirshodaya: signs that rise with the head first, considered auspicious for new ventures</note> brings the fulfillment of desires. Specifically, the 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, and 3rd houses are noted; Aquarius and Pisces are also Head-rising signs. Even if a sign is generally criticized, if it is the "Head-rising" sign of the direction one intends to travel, it is a favorable Ascendant. 

Journeying during the rising of one's birth sign <note>Janmarashi</note> brings success, but some say one should not travel exactly when the birth sign rises. It is auspicious when the Sun is in the 2nd house from the birth sign (known as the *Veshi* position). 

**Auspicious Signs for Travel:**
- **By Day (Day-strength signs):** 5, 6, 7, 8, 11, 12 <note>Leo, Virgo, Libra, Scorpio, Aquarius, Pisces</note>
- **By Night (Night-strength signs):** 2, 1, 9, 4, 3, 10 <note>Taurus, Aries, Sagittarius, Cancer, Gemini, Capricorn</note>

It is best to travel during a "Movable" sign <note>Chara Rashi: Aries, Cancer, Libra, Capricorn</note>. A "Dual" sign <note>Gemini, Virgo, Sagittarius, Pisces</note> is middling, and a "Fixed" sign <note>Taurus, Leo, Scorpio, Aquarius</note> should be avoided. Those Ascendants joined by benefic planets are to be accepted. The 4th, 8th, and 2nd houses are excellent Ascendants. One should not travel when the Ascendant is under the control of an enemy planet to one's own birth sign.

### The Functional Roles of Planets
Now, the definitions of the Protector, the Increaser, the Leader, the Doer, and the Sub-leader:
- **The Protector (Rakshaka):** A planet in the 2nd house from the birth Sun, joined with benefics, becomes the Protector in the travel chart.
- **The Increaser (Vardhaka):** A planet in the 10th house from the birth Ascendant, joined with benefics, is the Increaser.
- **The Leader (Tan-nayaka):** A planet in an "Upachaya" house <note>The 3rd, 6th, 10th, or 11th houses of growth</note> from the birth Moon, joined with benefics, is called the Leader.
- **The Doer (Karaka):** Planets situated in the birth Ascendant, the 4th house, the 10th house, or the 11th house are mutually defined as "Doers." A planet in its own sign or exaltation is also a Doer.
- **The Sub-leader (Upanayaka):** A planet in the 10th house from a "Doer" planet, or one situated in its exaltation or trine in the 9th house, is known as the Sub-leader. These Protectors and Increasers are determined from the birth chart.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

The lords of the signs <note>original: "nayakah"</note>, when placed in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon at the time of departure</term>, allow one to undertake a journey without hesitation for the sake of profit. Even an auspicious planet can become harmful, or a harmful one can become fruitless, depending on the specific planetary positions and the protective strength of the directions. The Lord of the Direction <note>original: "diggishvara"</note> is significant if positioned "on the forehead" <note>meaning the direction one is facing during travel</note> or if endowed with directional strength <term>Digbala: the specific strength a planet gains when placed in a certain cardinal direction</term>. If such a planet is positioned in a quadrant <term>Kendra: the 1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses of a horoscope</term>, it grants victory and wealth, but it may also cause imprisonment or death for the traveler.

The Lords of the Directions are as follows: the Sun, Venus, Mars, Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note>, Saturn, the Moon, Mercury, and Jupiter. If the Lord of the Direction is situated "on the forehead" <note>facing the traveler</note>, the traveler shall not return again. Specifically:
* The Sun causes fear of fire.
* Mars <note>original: "lohita," the Red Planet</note> causes the depletion of the treasury.
* Mercury <note>original: "shashankatanaya," the son of the Moon</note> brings victory over enemies.
* Jupiter causes the destruction of the army.
* Saturn <note>original: "bhaskaranandana," the son of the Sun</note> brings death to the king.
* Venus <note>original: "viprarat," the king of the learned</note> brings disease.

These are the various fruits of the planets <note>original: "khechara," literally 'sky-goers'</note>. Even a single Venus, if placed in the Ascendant on an enemy's day, is not beneficial. Conversely, even a malefic planet is auspicious if the journey occurs on a friend's day.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

### Special Considerations for Travel
Now, here are the specific details: A waning Moon <note>original: "apūrṇaḥ"</note> in the Ascendant <term>Lagna: the zodiac sign rising on the eastern horizon</term> brings sorrow. If the Moon is weak and positioned in the sixth house <note>the house of enemies and illness</note> in the signs of Cancer or Taurus <note>original: "karka go"</note>, it loses its ability to ward off evil results. 

The Sun, when poorly placed, causes fear of the government or authorities. Venus, when joined with the Moon, causes loss of wealth. Jupiter causes displacement from one's position or home. Mercury <note>original: "shashi-suta," son of the moon</note> brings great distress and faults. Saturn <note>original: "surya-suta," son of the sun</note> certainly brings death, and Mars <note>original: "bhu-suta," son of the earth</note> brings injury by weapons. Therefore, a wise person should always avoid traveling when these planets are in conjunction with the Moon. However, Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> is productive of good results during a journey if he is moving toward the destination. Ketu <note>the South Node of the Moon</note> is auspicious if positioned in the direction one is leaving behind.

### Specific Results of the Weekdays and Planetary Hours
Now, the individual results: If one travels on the day or during the specific time-segment <term>Amshaka: a divisional portion of a sign</term> of the Sun, the traveler becomes tormented by worries and loses wealth, much like a man who loses his money to a courtesan. 

If the journey occurs during the rising or the time-segment of the Moon, the traveler soon becomes dejected, like a man who encounters a harsh woman whose youth has faded. 

If one travels on the day or during the hour of Mars, the traveler faces imprisonment, death, or loss of wealth, suffering like one who serves a sinful master or is obsessed with another's wife. 

A journey during the Ascendant, time-segment, or day of Mercury pleases the man immensely; it is like being with a noble woman who is devoted, clever in her actions, and filled with affection. 

During the days or time-segments of Jupiter, a journey brings benefits and fulfills desired cravings, like a devoted wife who is favorable to one's mind and increases one's happiness. 

A journey during the rising or time-segments of Venus pleases the traveler through various successful deeds and intelligence, like a playful woman who, under the influence of desire, provides many enjoyments. 

Travel during the days or segments of Saturn causes faults such as the severing of life-breaths <note>extreme danger or death</note>; it is like being deluded by a woman who is attached to another man but is pursued out of infatuation.

### The Wings of Life and Death
Now, regarding the "Living" and "Dead" sides <note>original: "Jiva-mrita-paksha"</note>: The constellation occupied by Rahu is called the "Scissor" <term>Kartari: a configuration that 'cuts' the efficacy of a house</term>. The thirteen constellations ahead of it constitute the "Side of Life" <note>Jivapaksha</note>. If the Sun is in the "Side of Death" and the Moon is in the "Side of Life," the journey is auspicious. If both the Sun and Moon are in the "Side of Life," that is also auspicious. If the Sun is in the "Side of Life" and the Moon... <note>text breaks off</note>

Travel is not auspicious during the **Dead Side** <note>mṛtapakaṣa; a division of the zodiacal circle used in martial astrology</note>. If both the Sun and the Moon have entered the Dead Side, then a journey undertaken at that time will result in great destruction. The Sun is the lord of the **Defender** <note>sthāyī; the one who stays in their position or fort</note>, while the Moon is the lord of the **Attacker** <note>yāyī; the one who moves or marches</note>. Victory belongs to whichever party is positioned in the **Living Side** <note>jīvapakṣa</note>. 

For example: if Rahu <note>the North Node of the Moon</note> is currently in the constellation of *Anuradha*, then the "Curved Blade" <note>vakra-kartarī; a specific astrological configuration</note> extends from *Jyeshtha* to *Bharani*. This constitutes the Living Side. From *Vishakha* onwards for thirteen constellations is the Dead Side. *Kruttika* is the 15th constellation and is considered "set" or hidden. Here, if both parties are in the Living Side, a peace treaty should be made; if both are in the Dead Side, it brings ruin to both. This is explained in detail in the *Narapati-jayacharya* <note>a famous 12th-century Sanskrit text on military omens and victory</note>.

**The Mixed Circle:** *Mula, Shatabhisha, Ardra, Rohini*. On Wednesdays, and on the 2nd, 6th, and 10th lunar days. At the start of a battle during these times, a peace treaty <note>sandhi</note> should be formed. 

The Living and Dead sides must certainly be investigated for both warriors. This is especially mandatory for "Cruel Journeys" <note>military invasions or aggressive marches</note>; it is not as strictly necessary for auspicious/peaceful travels. One should always examine the Mixed Circle in matters of war and deeds, as well as the movement of Rahu. It is not always applicable for peaceful journeys, but it must be applied to both sides in aggressive marches, considering the strength of Rahu, the "Six Limbs" of the Wheel of Time, the "Fire of Death" of the Moon, and the "Fire of Death" of the Sun.

When the Sun is situated in the "Virtue" house, it is auspicious for Wealth and Liberation. When the Moon is in the "Wealth" house, it is recommended for Virtue, Liberation, and Wealth. When in the "Desire" house, it is beautiful for Virtue, Liberation, and Wealth. When in the "Liberation" house, only the "Virtue" house is spoken of as auspicious. A zero portion <note>shunyansha: an inauspicious void</note> in the day or the lunar mansion should be avoided.

One should observe the planetary positions in a clockwise direction. The duration of influence for Saturn is half a watch <note>yamardha: approximately 1.5 hours</note>; one should not travel toward the direction where he resides at that time. Now, the "All-Sun Yoga" <note>a mathematical formula for success</note>: take the values of the Lunar Date (Tithi), the Day (Vara), and the Name-initial of the person. Place them in three positions and multiply them respectively by 2, 3, and 4. Then divide them respectively by 6, 7, and 8. If the remainder is zero in the first position, there is loss; zero in the middle means fear; zero at the end means death. If all three positions result in zero, death is certain. If there is a remainder of one in all three positions, victory is assured. The Lunar Dates are counted from the first day of the bright fortnight. Alternatively, the sum of the Date, Day, and Lunar Mansion is placed in three spots and multiplied by 7, 8, and 3.

Now regarding the "Great Obstacle" (Mahadala) and "Cloud-Error" (Abhrama): Count the lunar mansions from the Sun's current mansion. Divide by 7. If the remainder is 2 or 7, it is Mahadala. If the remainder is 3 or 6, it is Abhrama. Both are considered blameworthy. Abhrama is specifically forbidden for travel. Mahadala should always be avoided in travel, setting machinery, plowing with a hara, battle, theft, making treaties, and the construction of wells, gardens, or ponds. However, it is said there is no fault in using it for auspicious marriage rituals if done with care. Now, the "Hindvara": Count the lunar mansions from the Sun, add the Lunar Date (from the bright fortnight) and the Day of the week. Divide by 9. If the remainder is 7, it is Hindvara, which is excellent for departure. Now, the "Ghabadaka": Count the lunar mansions from the Sun...

## Now, the Analysis of This

In war, marriage, the worship of the <term>Kumari</term><note>A ritual involving the worship of a young prepubescent girl as a goddess</note>, in travel, and in the service of kings, a wise person should contemplate the results of these harmful influences (<term>Ghata-phala</term>). However, one should not worry about these during auspicious ceremonies like weddings or the <term>Chuda</term><note>The first tonsure or haircutting ceremony for a child</note> ritual. 

Furthermore, it is stated that when the stars are free from the <term>Parigha</term><note>An astrological obstruction or "bolt"</note> defect—specifically the stars <term>Anuradha</term>, <term>Hasta</term>, <term>Pushya</term>, and <term>Ashwini</term>—travel is declared auspicious in all directions by the learned. 

Similarly, regarding the <term>Lagna</term><note>The Ascendant or rising sign</note>: if it faces the direction of travel, there is victory. If it is to the right, the result is middling; if to the left, there is loss; and if it is behind, there is great fear. The <term>Chakri</term><note>A specific planetary configuration</note> situated in the center and its divisions are forbidden. If the 8th house from the birth sign or the birth ascendant is occupied by a malefic planet, or if the lords of those houses are in the ascendant, such a journey should be understood as bringing misfortune (<term>Arishta</term>).

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments
<note>Original title: Muhurtasindhu</note>

For Brahmins, success comes through auspicious lunar mansions; for others, through the omens of birds; for common folk, through favorable moments <term>Muhurta: a unit of time approximately 48 minutes long</term>. Here, the purification of the prescribed stars is declared for all. Now, regarding the planetary combinations: when Venus, Mercury, and Jupiter are situated in the cardines <note>1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th houses</note> or trines <note>1st, 5th, or 9th houses</note>, the "Yoga" and "Adhiyoga" combinations are formed. From the combination of one, two, or three of these planets, the results are safety, victory over enemies, and gain of wealth. Specifically, with one planet, there is safety; with two, safety and the destruction of enemies; with three, safety, destruction of enemies, and the acquisition of wealth.

Now, regarding **Vijayadashami** <note>The "Victorious Tenth" festival, celebrating the victory of Good over Evil</note>: The tenth lunar day of the bright half of the month of Ashvina is called "Vijaya." It is the supreme time for a king’s expedition to ensure victory. If this day coincides with the Shravana nakshatra <note>The star associated with Lord Vishnu</note>, it is even more effective for achieving desired goals. Now, regarding the specific moment called "Vijaya": it is the eleventh Muhurta of the day. Alternatively, it is that time just past twilight when the stars are slightly visible; this time, named Vijaya, is the accomplisher of all goals. Now, if the lunar day <term>Tithi</term> and other factors are forbidden, but the rising sign <term>Lagna</term> is strong, one should proceed by using the power of "Dohada" <note>Ritual offerings or "cravings" satisfied to appease the deities of the time</note>.

Now, regarding the ritual requirements: if a specific food is mentioned, one should either look at it or touch it. Now, the **Procedure for Departure** <note>original: "Prasthanavidhi"</note>: At an auspicious moment, one should worship with scents and unbroken rice. One should take a sacred thread, weapons, honey, and two myrobalan fruits <note>original: "Amalaka"</note> to a temple or a place free from the sound of musical instruments. The symbolic departure <note>a ritual "head start" where one moves a short distance and waits for the full journey</note> should be at a distance of 500 <term>Dhanus</term> <note>A unit of measure, roughly 6 feet per Dhanus</note>, or 200 Dhanus, or even 10 Dhanus from the house to another building. Once the departure is initiated from the house toward the intended direction, it must be carried out with effort. One should avoid milk for 3 days and avoid <term>shaving</term> <note>original: "Kshauram"</note> for 5 days.

# The Ocean of Auspicious Moments

<page-num>161</page-num>

->**The Ocean of Auspicious Moments**<-

Sexual intercourse should be avoided for seven days prior to a journey. If one is incapable of such restraint or in cases of extreme necessity, one must at least avoid the following on the day of departure: shaving, anger, weeping, eating meat, applying oil, consuming jaggery <note>unrefined cane sugar</note>, and sexual intercourse. He who departs in the morning after having engaged in intercourse at night shall not obtain the fruits of his journey and will return only with great difficulty. As long as one is traveling the road, until the task is accomplished, or until one returns, one should avoid intercourse. However, there is no fault in this during the "season" <note>the fertile period following a woman's menstruation</note> because the strength of the Vedic injunction <note>the religious duty to conceive</note> prevails over other rules.

A journey is also prohibited during unseasonable rain. This refers to rain occurring during the four months beginning with Pausha <note>approximately December to April</note>. **Narada** states: "When there is lightning, thunder, and rain out of season—these three types of portents—a King should not set out for seven nights." If one must go, one should perform a peace-offering ritual <term>Shanti: a ritual to avert evil or bad luck</term> and gaze upon the Sun and Moon.

### The Procedure for Departure

Now, the method of departure: With enthusiasm increased by the sounds of conches, flutes, lutes, and kettledrums; accompanied by banners, fly-whisks, and parasols; dressed in white unguents, garments, and a turban; having gratified the sacred fire with oblations and the twice-born <note>Brahmins</note> with gifts of cows, land, and gold; having offered salutations <insert>corrected from: namaskarutya</insert> to elders; and having cheered his wife, friends, and sons—the King should depart. Having bowed to his personal deity and the Lord of his direction <insert>corrected from: svadagishvaram</insert> with faith, wearing white garlands and fine clothes <insert>corrected from: varastrah</insert>, he should set his foot forward in accordance with his breath <note>referring to the flow of breath through the nostrils, a practice in Svara Yoga</note>, extending the right foot first.

Having first raised the right foot and walked thirty-two steps, he should mount a divine vehicle <insert>corrected from: dipyayanam</insert>. After first giving a vessel of sesame, clarified butter, gold, and copper to an excellent astrologer, he should set forth. Departing from a temple, the house of his teacher, his own home, or the home of his chief wife, and having eaten sacrificial food with permission, he should proceed while seeing and hearing auspicious things.

The eight auspicious items are said to be: a full water-pot, a banner, a parasol, a lamp, a conch, a fly-whisk, gold, and the autumn sun.

Furthermore, regarding the days of the week and the breath: On the days of Jupiter, Saturn, the Sun, and Mars <note>original abbreviations: Gu, Sha, Ra, Bhau</note>, the right breath is auspicious. On the days of the Moon and Venus <note>original abbreviations: Chandra, Shu</note>, the left breath is auspicious. When leaving, the left is auspicious; when entering, the right is auspicious. In cases of necessity, one may use the **Abhijit** moment <note>a short period around midday considered universally auspicious</note> or the period after the forenoon, at midday, toward the east, or in the afternoon...

At midnight, if Mars is in the west, or during the Vishti <term>Vishti: an inauspicious period in the lunar calendar</term>, or on Saturday, there is fear. One is not harmed by the Vyatipata <term>Vyatipata: a specific unlucky astrological yoga</term> if the Sun is situated to the south. If one travels with the day-lord <note>the planet ruling the day of the week</note> behind them or to the right, it is favorable.

The "Siddha" <note>perfected or successful</note> shadows for the planets are as follows: eight paces for Mercury, nine for Mars, seven for Jupiter, eleven for the Sun, and four and a half paces for the Moon, Saturn, and Venus. At such a time, the moment <note>Muhurta</note> is endowed with all virtues for the success of all tasks. In this specific calculation, the primary sages like Garga have stated that the usual purification of the five limbs of the calendar <term>Panchanga: Tithi, Vara, Nakshatra, Yoga, Karana</term> and the strength of the moon are not required.

The shadow lengths (in fingers/inches) for success are: 4, 16, 7, 15, 2, 12, and 11 <note>represented by chronograms: Krita, Nripa, Muni, Tithi, Paksha, Dvadasha, Rudra</note>. Others state the measurements for the Sun etc. as: Sun 20, Moon 16, Mars 15, Mercury 14, Jupiter 13, Venus 12, and Saturn 12 <term>Angula: a traditional unit of measurement roughly equal to a finger's width</term>.
